Prospectus.Asthisisasummary,itdoesnotcontainalltheinformationthatmaybeimportant
to you. You should read the entire Prospectus before you decide to invest in our H Shares.

OVERVIEW
We focus on the commercial deployment of mining autonomous driving solutions in the
mining industry and were among the early entrants in autonomous mining transportation. Our
solutions are designed for large-scale open-pit mines with complex mining environment, limited
labor supply and stringent safety requirements. According to Frost & Sullivan, we ranked first in
China’s commercial vehicle intelligent driving market by revenue in 2025 and were also the largest
provider of mining autonomous driving solutions in China by the number of active autonomous
mining trucks as of December 31, 2025, with a market share of approximately 37.6% by revenue
in 2025.As of December 31, 2025, our deployed fleet comprised 2,580 active autonomous mining
trucks.
We provide fully integrated solutions for large-scale mining operations through two core
solution suites: (i) Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions
(ORCASTRA) and (ii) Mining Digitalization Solutions (Conductor Plus). We collaborate with
qualified OEM partners to manufacture autonomous mining trucks based on our specifications,
while we develop and integrate the autonomous driving systems and core control components.
These trucks are deployed on-site as part of an integrated solution, and we primarily generate
revenue from service fees charged to mining companies or their appointed contractors. For further
details, see “— Our Solutions and Business Model.”
We have recognized the potential for scaled adoption of autonomous mining and moved
quickly to establish presence across the China’s mining autonomous driving solution market.As of
December 31, 2025, our solutions were deployed in 19 of all the 41 open-pit coal mines with
approvedannualcapacityexceeding10milliontonnes,andsevenoutofthe12largestopen-pitcoal
mines in terms of approved annual capacity in China. Our established track record with leading
mining companies has supported the development of a stable customer base, as evidenced by a
100%retentionrateacrossallofourendcustomergroupsforthreeconsecutiveyearsbetween2023
and2025.Weserved13,24and52customersin2023,2024and2025,respectively.AsofDecember
31, 2025, our solutions have been deployed in nine out of all the 11 of China’s autonomous mining
deployments operating fleets of over 100 autonomous mining trucks. In addition, as of December
31, 2025, the fleet deployed at a single mining site where our solutions are in operation has grown
to over 500 autonomous mining trucks, representing the largest autonomous mining truck fleet
deployed at a single mine globally. This expansion reflects our customers’ continued confidence in
our solutions and their ongoing expansion of deployments with us as their operations scale.
A Market with Significant Growth Potential
Miningisoneofthefewautonomousdrivingapplicationsthathasalreadyreachedmeaningful
commercial scale. According to Frost & Sullivan, China’s mining autonomous driving solution
market is entering a rapid scale-up phase, with penetration of autonomous mining trucks expected
to increase from approximately 12% in 2025 to over 50% by 2030, while the market size reached
RMB3.8 billion in 2025, representing a CAGR of 171.4% from 2021 to 2025. We ranked first in
China by revenue with a market share of 37.6% in 2025. Globally, demand is also increasing in
major mining regions such asAustralia, Canada and Chile, with the market expected to grow from
US$1.0 billion in 2025 to US$7.3 billion by 2030. For further details, see “Industry Overview.”

OUR SOLUTIONS AND BUSINESS MODELS
We offer two core solution suites (i) Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks
Products and Solutions (ORCASTRA), and (ii) Mining Digitalization Solutions (Conductor Plus).
During the Track Record Period, the majority of our revenue was generated from Closed-
EnvironmentAutonomous MiningTrucks Products and Solutions (ORCASTRA).The following sets
forth a summary of Closed-EnvironmentAutonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions under
both customer-provided fleet and Company-provided fleet models, including their respective fee
and revenue models, for details, see “Business — What We Offer.”
ORCASTRA — Customer-Provided Fleet Model
 Scope of services: We offer hardware-software products and services focused on autonomous
technology layer, such as remote driving assistance, autonomous dispatch, remote technical
support, ongoing software updates to the autonomous systems deployed on customer-owned
trucks. We do not assume responsibility for daily truck maintenance and repair, as those
obligations remain with the customer or their appointed contractors. Upon completion or
termination of a project, the handling of hardware and software, including any rights to
retrieve hardware or uninstall software, shall be governed by the applicable agreements.
 Target Customers: Mining companies or their contractors that already or prefer to own or
lease mining trucks.
 Fee and revenue model: Under this model, for customers who purchase trucks from us, we
charge usage-based service fees on top of the truck purchase price. These fees are generally
linked to the volume of material transported, with pricing commonly calculated on a
per-cubic-meterbasis;theratemayvaryacrossdifferentminingdeploymentsbasedonfactors
such as haul distance, slope conditions, and overall site complexity. In 2024 and 2025, we
began to explore two new fee models: (i) a predetermined per-truck fee based on the number
of mining trucks involved in the processes, with the per-truck fee varying across different
mining deployments (the “per-truck fee model”), and (ii) a one-time fee for the entire
deployment(the“one-timefeemodel,”asdescribedbelow).Beginninginlate2024,wetested
the per-truck fee model in selected projects to assess its commercial viability and scalability.
During theTrack Record Period, several customers adopted the per-truck fee model following
our promotional efforts, recognizing our technological capabilities and considering that the
model better aligns with its commercial objectives. In the first half of 2025, under our
customer-provided fleet model, we also piloted the one-time fee model, under which fees are
not linked to transportation volume or per-vehicle revenue. Instead, we deploy our system
across a customer’s mining site, integrate our solutions into its mining trucks, and collect a
one-time service fee for the deployment and continued use of our technology.Throughout the
Track Record Period, the one-off revenue from the sales of autonomous mining trucks
equipped with our solutions has accounted for a substantial majority of our revenue under
customer-provided fleet model. Under this model, if customers do not purchase trucks from
us,wewouldnotrecognizerevenuefromsalesofautonomousminingtrucks,andourrevenue
from the customer-provided fleet model may decline or fluctuate. See “Risk Factors — Risks
RelatingtoOurBusinessandIndustry—Ourrevenuefromthecustomer-providedfleetmodel
may decline or fluctuate if customers do not purchase autonomous mining trucks from us.”
ORCASTRA — Company-Provided Fleet Model
 Scope of services: We offer hardware-software products and autonomous truck-related
full-lifecycle services, spanning both the autonomous technology layer and truck
management.Inadditiontoallservicesprovidedunderthecustomer-providedfleetmodel,we
assume responsibility for daily maintenance and repair of the autonomous mining trucks we
supply.
 Target Customers: Primarily mining companies or their contractors that prefer not to
purchase and manage their own fleet of mining trucks.
 Fee and revenue model: Customers typically pay us on a recurring basis for our mining
autonomous driving services. Fees are generally linked to the volume of material transported,
with pricing most commonly calculated on a per-cubic-meter or per-tonne basis. The
applicable rate may vary across different mining deployments, depending on factors such as
haul distance, slope conditions, costs associated with maintaining a self-owned fleet, and
overall site complexity.

BUSINESS SUSTAINABILITY AND PATH TO PROFITABILITY
We have not recorded net profits during the Track Record Period and expect to continue to
incur net losses in the near term. We first deployed our solutions to mining sites in July 2020. Our
accumulated losses were primarily attributable to the heavy upfront investment associated with our
Company-provided fleet model in the early stages, sustained research and development efforts to
establish the technological foundation of our solutions, and relatively high customer acquisition
costs in a nascent industry. In addition, we adopted a proactive market expansion strategy during
early commercialization, prioritizing rapid deployment and broad coverage to secure high-quality
customers,whichincreasedourinitialcostofrevenue.Thesefactorsledtogrosslossesin2023and
relatively thin gross margins in 2024 and 2025.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, we incurred losses of RMB333.7 million, RMB390.1 million and
RMB515.6 million, respectively. Our adjusted net loss (non-HKFRS measure) for these years was
RMB283.9million,RMB303.3millionandRMB484.5million,respectively.Theselossesprimarily
reflect our strategic investments to establish the technological and commercial foundation of our
solutions.
Looking forward, we expect to improve profitability through business model transformation,
revenue scale and cost optimization. In particular, we are expanding our customer base through
benchmark deployments and strategic partnerships with leading mining groups, which have
supported customer-led expansion across additional mining sites. At the same time, we are
transitioning from the capital-intensive Company-provided fleet model to the more capital-light
customer-providedfleetmodel,underwhichcustomerspurchaseorleasevehicleswhileweprovide
autonomous driving technologies, software support and services. In 2025, revenue under the
customer-provided fleet model accounted for 56.8% of our total revenue, as compared to 46.0% in
2024 and 41.7% in 2023.
We are also realizing economies of scale as our deployments expand. From 2023 to 2025, our
annual transport distance increased from 4.6 million to 61.8 million kilometers and annual material
volume transported increased from 30.6 million to 308.0 million cubic meters. In addition,
increasing procurement volumes have strengthened our bargaining power with suppliers and
improved our cost structure.
At the same time, we are rationalizing R&D while sustaining innovation by focusing on
modular productization and reusing validated components across deployments. While we continue
to invest in areas such as AI algorithms, intelligent production management and hardware
development, we expect R&D expenses as a percentage of revenue to decline over time as
deploymentsscaleandcustomizationdecreases.Webelievetheseeffortswillgraduallyimproveour
operating efficiency and support our path toward sustainable profitability. For further details, see
“Business — Business Sustainability and Path to Profitability.”

Non-HKFRS Measures
Tosupplementourconsolidatedstatementsofprofitorlosswhicharepresentedinaccordance
with HKFRS Accounting Standards, we use adjusted net loss (non-HKFRS measure) for the year,
EBITDA (non-HKFRS measure), and adjusted EBITDA (non-HKFRS measure) as additional
financialmeasures,whicharenotrequiredby,orpresentedinaccordancewith,HKFRSAccounting
Standards.
We believe that these non-HKFRS measures facilitate comparisons of operating performance
from year to year and company to company. We believe that these measures provide useful
information to investors in understanding and evaluating our consolidated results of operations in
thesamemannerastheyhelpmanagement.However,presentationofadjustednetloss(non-HKFRS
measure) for the year, EBITDA (non-HKFRS measure), and adjusted EBITDA (non-HKFRS
measure)maynotbecomparabletosimilarlytitledmeasurespresentedbyothercompanies.Theuse
of these non-HKFRS measures has limitations as an analytical tool, and investors should not
considertheminisolationfrom,orassubstituteforanalysisof,ourresultsofoperationsorfinancial
condition as reported under HKFRS Accounting Standards. We define adjusted net loss (non-
HKFRS measure) as loss for the year, adjusted for share-based payment, listing expenses and fair
value changes on financial liabilities at FVTPL. Share-based compensation relates to the
share-based awards that we grant to participants of our share incentive schemes and is a non-cash
expense. Listing expenses refer to expenses incurred related to the Global Offering. Fair value
changes on financial liabilities at FVTPLarise from the shares with preferred rights that we issued
to certain pre-IPO investors in the past and such financial liabilities been re-designated from
liabilities to equity as a result of the automatic conversion into ordinary shares which was
completedinthefirsthalfof2025.Thesechangesarenon-cashinnature.Fordetailsofsuchshares
with special rights, see “History, Development and Corporate Structure — Pre-IPO Investments”.

capital consumption, with increases in trade and other payables partially offsetting funding needs.
For details, see “Financial Information — Liquidity and Capital Resources”.

RISK FACTORS
Our business and the Global Offering involve certain risks as set out in “Risk Factors” in this
Prospectus. You should read that section in its entirety carefully before you decide to invest in our
Shares. Some of the major risks we face include: (i) The success of our business depends on our
ability to retain existing customers, acquire new ones, and expand the adoption of our solutions
withinourcustomerbase.Afailuretoaccomplishtheseobjectivescouldseverelyharmourfinancial
condition and operational performance; (ii) we have a limited operating history, which makes it
difficult to evaluate our business and prospects, and our historical growth may not be indicative of
our future performance; (iii) the industries that we operate in are highly competitive. If we fail to
compete with our competitors, our business, results of operations and financial condition may be
materially and adversely affected; (iv) our business relies heavily on the application of autonomy
intheminingmarketsthatutilizeoursolutions.Thesizeofouraddressablemarketsandthedemand
for our solutions may not increase as rapidly as we anticipate due to a variety of factors. A
slowdown in the growth of these markets could negatively impact our business, financial condition
and results of operations; (v) if we are unable to develop new solutions that adapt to changing
market demand and customer needs in a cost-effective and timely manner, our future business,
results of operations, financial condition and competitive position would be materially and
adversely affected. For details, see “Risk Factors”.
COMPETITIVE LANDSCAPE
The market for commercial vehicle intelligent driving solution in China reached
approximately RMB14.0 billion in 2025. Our Group ranked first among all commercial vehicle
intelligent driving solution providers in terms of market share by revenue, capturing approximately
10.2% of the total market.As of the end of 2025, our Group ranked first in the mining autonomous
driving solution market, with a 55.5% market share based on an active fleet of 2,580 autonomous
vehicles. For details, see “Industry Overview.”

WORKING CAPITAL
Taking into account the financial resources available to us, including existing cash and cash
equivalents, available bank facilities and the estimated net proceeds from the Global Offering, our
Directors believe that we have sufficient working capital for our present requirements and for the
next 12 months from the date of this Prospectus. After making reasonable inquiries of our
management about our working capital, the Sole Sponsor concurs with the views of our Directors.
We intend to finance our future working capital requirements and capital expenditures primarily
from cash expected to be generated from operating activities, bank facilities and funds raised from
financing activities, including the net proceeds we will receive from the Global Offering.
DIVIDEND
During the Track Record Period, no dividends have been declared and paid by us.
Any dividends we pay will be determined at the absolute discretion of our Board which will
be subject to our Article of Association and the PRC Company Law, as well as the Company’s
Shareholders meeting approval processes, taking into account factors including our actual and
expected results of operations, cash flow and financial position, general business conditions and
business strategies, expected working capital requirements and future expansion plans, legal,
regulatory and other contractual restrictions, and other factors from time to time that our Board
deems to be appropriate. Our Shareholders in a general meeting may approve any declaration of
dividendsrecommendedbyourBoard.AccordingtothePRClaw,anyfuturenetprofitthatwemake
will have to be first applied to make up for our historically accumulated losses, after which we will
be obliged to allocate 10% of our net profit to our statutory common reserve fund until such fund
has reached more than 50% of our registered capital. Distributable profits are our after-tax profits
less any recovery of accumulated losses and appropriations to statutory that we are required to
make. As advised by our PRC Legal Advisor, we are unable to pay dividend under the applicable
PRC law and regulations as of December 31, 2025, in view of our accumulated losses. As of the
Latest Practicable Date, we do not have any predetermined dividend payout ratio or fixed dividend
policy.

ones, and expand the adoption of our solutions within our customer base. A failure to
accomplish these objectives could severely harm our financial condition and operational
performance.

or alterations in our customers’ business needs or operations.

our revenue. Customer H was our largest customer in 2024 and 2025 and contributed RMB22.6

representing 8.3%, 54.5% and 35.7% of our total revenue in the same year, respectively.According

payments to us could materially and adversely affect our revenue, cash flows, financial condition
and results of operations. For further details, see “Business — Our Customers.”
If we fail to effectively adapt to evolving industry trends, innovate our offerings, or develop

On August 9, 2023, the U.S. government issued Executive Order 14105 titled Addressing
United States Investments in Certain National Security Technologies and Products in Countries of
Concern (“E.O. 14105”) and the U.S. Department of the Treasury (“Treasury”) published an
advanced notice of proposed rulemaking providing a proposed framework for outbound investment
controls focused on China, including the Hong Kong and Macau SARs. On June 21, 2024,Treasury
issued a proposed rule for this framework. On October 28, 2024, Treasury issued a Final Rule (the
“Final Rule”; and such program as in effect on the date hereof pursuant to the Final Rule, the
“OISP”) setting forth the OISP regulations that implement E.O. 14105. The OISP took effect on
January 2, 2025. The Final Rule targets investments by U.S. persons that involve persons and
entities associated with “countries of concern,” currently China, including the SARs of Hong Kong
and Macau. The OISP imposes investment (1) prohibitions and (2) notification requirements on
certain actions by U.S. persons, including the extent to which such U.S. persons (including, among
others,U.S.-incorporatedentities,U.S.citizensandpermanentresidentswhereverlocated,branches

Pursuant to the PRC Individual Income Tax Law (《中華人民共和國個人所得稅法》),
non-PRC resident individuals are subject to a 20% PRC individual income tax on their dividend
income derived from China and we are required to withhold such tax from our dividend payments.
If there is an applicable tax treaty to avoid double taxation and taxation evasion between China and
the jurisdiction where the foreign individual resides, the applicable tax rate shall be determined in
accordance with such tax treaty. Considering the applicable tax rate on dividends is usually 10%
according to tax treaties or tax agreements, and that the number of stockholders is large for a listed
company, to simplify the tax administration, generally a domestic non-foreign-investment
enterprise with shares listed in Hong Kong can withhold dividend income tax at a rate of 10%.
There remains uncertainty as to whether gains realized by non-PRC resident individuals on
disposition of H Shares are subject to the PRC individual income tax.
Pursuant to the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (《中華人民共和國企業所得稅法》) and
other applicable PRC tax rules and regulations, non-PRC resident enterprises that do not have
establishments or premises in the PRC, or have establishments or premises in the PRC but their
income is not related to such establishments or premises are subject to a 10% PRC enterprise
incometaxrateondividendincomereceivedfromaPRCcompanyandgainsrealizeduponthesale
or other dispositions of equity interest in a PRC company. For details, see “Regulatory Overview
— Regulations on Taxation.” There remains substantial uncertainty as to the interpretation and

WAIVER IN RESPECT OF MANAGEMENT PRESENCE IN HONG KONG
Pursuant to Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules, our Company must have a sufficient management
presence in Hong Kong. This normally means that at least two of our executive Directors must be
ordinarily resident in Hong Kong. Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules further provides that the
requirement in Rule 8.12 of the Listing Rules may be waived by having regard to, among other
considerations, our arrangements for maintaining regular communication with the Stock Exchange.
Our Group’s management, business operations and assets are primarily based outside Hong
Kong. The principal management headquarters and senior management of our Group are primarily
based in China. Our Directors consider that either by means of relocation of existing executive
Directors or the appointment of executive Directors who will be ordinarily resident in Hong Kong
would not be beneficial to, or appropriate for, our Group and therefore would not be in the best
interests of our Company and our Shareholders as a whole. Therefore, we do not have, and do not
contemplate to have, in the foreseeable future, sufficient management presence in Hong Kong for
the purpose of satisfying the requirements under Rules 8.12 and 19A.15 of the Listing Rules.
Accordingly, pursuant to Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules, we have applied to the Stock
Exchange for, and the Stock Exchange has granted us, a waiver from strict compliance with the
requirements under Rule 8.12 and Rule 19A.15 of the Listing Rules. We will ensure that there is
a regular and effective communication between us and the Stock Exchange by way of the following
arrangements:

our Company complies with the Listing Rules at all times. The two Authorized
Representatives are Mr. Lan and Ms. Chan Wing Yan (陳詠欣) (“Ms. Chan”). Each of
our Authorized Representatives has provided his/her contact details to the Stock
Exchange, and will be available to meet with the Stock Exchange within a reasonable
time frame upon the request of the Stock Exchange and will be readily contactable by
phone, facsimile (if applicable) and email. Each of the Authorized Representatives is
authorized to communicate on our behalf with the Stock Exchange;

CHINA’S COMMERCIAL VEHICLE INTELLIGENT DRIVING MARKET
The Evolvement of China’s Commercial Vehicle Intelligent Driving Market
Driving automation technology enables vehicles to operate without human intervention by
leveraging advanced sensors, control systems, and artificial intelligence, and usually refers
specifically to L4 and L5 autonomous driving systems that realize a high degree of automation and
full automation, respectively.According to SAE classification, autonomous driving ranges from L0
(no automation) to L5 (full automation). L0 represents manual driving, where the human driver is
entirely responsible for controlling the vehicle. L1 and L2 introduce driver assistance technologies,
where the system can assist with specific tasks like acceleration, steering, or braking, but human
oversight is still required. L3 allows for conditional automation, where the vehicle can take over
driving in certain conditions, but the driver must be ready to intervene when prompted. L4
representshighautomation,wherethevehiclecandriveautonomouslywithinaspecificoperational
design domain without human intervention, though it remains limited to certain environments. L5,
full automation, eliminates the need for any human oversight or control, allowing the vehicle to
operate autonomously in all environments. While autonomous driving, in particular L5 full
automation, on public roads remains a long-term goal, L4 autonomous driving has already been
realized in controlled environments such as mines, ports, and factories, where vehicles can operate
without human input under defined conditions.

Commercial vehicle intelligent driving can be broadly categorized into three types based on
their operating environments: urban roads, intercity roads, and closed environments. Urban-road
applications, such as last-mile delivery vehicles, face the highest technical challenges due to dense
traffic, frequent stops, and unpredictable interactions, and are mostly in pilot or early
commercialization stages. Intercity-road applications focus on autonomous trucks for highway
freight, benefiting from more structured routes but still requiring high safety standards at scale.
Closed environments, such as mines and ports, operate in controlled and predictable settings with
minimal external traffic, making them the most commercially mature segment and the earliest to
achieve large-scale deployment.
Intelligent driving is being adopted more rapidly in commercial vehicles than in passenger
cars, as commercial applications face fewer uncertainties in operating environments and clearer
regulatoryandeconomicconditions,whilebusinessusersprioritizeefficiencyandcostsavingswith
measurable returns on investment. In closed or semi-structured settings such as mines, ports, and
factories, autonomous trucks, tractors, and handling equipment have already proven their value by
improving safety, reducing labor dependence, and enabling stable, high-precision operations. With
clear economic benefits, including lower labor and fuel costs, fewer accidents, and higher
efficiency, intelligent driving is expected to continue expanding into sanitation, long-haul trucking,
and last-mile delivery as technology matures and labor constraints persist.

Mining: A High-Potential Application for Scaled Commercial Deployment of Autonomous
Driving
As a key pillar of the global resource supply chain, China’s mining industry has shown steady
growth, supported by industrial demand, manufacturing upgrades, and infrastructure development.
From 2021 to 2025, output of major nonferrous metals rose from 64.8 million tons to 81.8 million
tons, while raw coal production increased from 4.1 billion tons to 4.9 billion tons, underscoring
coal’s continued role in the national energy mix. Although quarry output declined amid the real
estate downturn, demand is expected to recover with infrastructure and urban renewal projects.
Against this backdrop of expanding operations, rising labor costs, and tighter safety and
environmental requirements, mining enterprises are increasingly adopting intelligent and
autonomous technologies to reduce costs, enhance safety, and support high-quality industry
development.

Mining is one of the most commercially viable and scalable application scenarios for
autonomous driving, benefiting from closed and highly structured operating environments that
support rapid deployment and around-the-clock operations, significantly improving productivity
and reducing downtime. While technical challenges such as dust, glare, and complex mining
environment require advanced sensor fusion, perception, and control systems, the industry has
alreadymovedbeyondproof-of-conceptintolarge-scalecommercialoperation.AsofDecember31,
2025, we had deployed 2,580 active autonomous mining trucks across all sites, delivering tangible
labor and efficiency gains. With China accelerating the transition toward intelligent, zero-accident,
and low-carbon mining, autonomous driving is expected to play an increasingly central role,
positioning mining as both a key proving ground and a major growth market, with a total
addressable market of approximately RMB185.0 billion.
CHINA’S MINING AUTONOMOUS DRIVING SOLUTION INDUSTRY
Growing Demand for Intelligent Mine Operations
Autonomous driving is accelerating China’s transition toward smart, automated mines by
modernizing mine-site transportation through the integration of autonomous mining trucks, IoT
infrastructure, cloud-based control platforms, and real-time dispatch systems.As a national priority
under China’s push for digital and intelligent industrial upgrades, “smart mine” development
focuses on improving productivity, safety, and environmental performance, with haulage playing a
criticalroleasthelinkbetweenextractionandprocessing.Autonomousdrivingenablescontinuous,
precise, and high-efficiency ore movement, reducing labor exposure, accident risk and production
losses. Open-pit mines, which dominate China’s coal and metal output and feature relatively
structured, point-to-point haulage routes, have emerged as the leading use case, offering immediate
and measurable gains in safety, uptime, and cost reduction.
Challenges Facing the Industry
Autonomous driving is becoming a necessity for mining as operators face persistently high
accident risks, rising labor costs, severe labor shortages, and increasing environmental pressure. In
2024, China recorded 0.059 fatalities per million tonnes of coal mined, while traditional haulage
typicallyrequires2-4driverspervehicle,withannualper-drivercostsofRMB100,000-150,000and
turnover rates exceeding 50% in some open-pit mines, especially in remote regions. Autonomous
mining trucks address these challenges by removing drivers from hazardous environments,
– 70 –

=== PAGE 80 ===
INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
operating around the clock, and improving efficiency, fuel economy, and headcount control, while
supporting low-carbon goals through intelligent dispatch and electrification. However, deployment
remains technically demanding: mining environments are unpaved, constantly changing, and
exposed to dust, snow, and low-light conditions, requiring robust sensor fusion, noise-resistant
perception, and reliable localization. As a result, only a small number of full-stack solution
providers, capable of integrating hardware, software, and operations, can deliver reliable, scalable
autonomous mining systems, creating a high barrier to entry and a clear advantage for integrated
players.
The Value Chain for Mining Autonomous Driving Solution Industry
The value chain for mining autonomous driving solution industry spans component supply,
system integration, and on-site operations.
 Upstream, the ecosystem includes component manufacturers, software providers, and
cloud service vendors that supply critical hardware, algorithms, and computing
infrastructure.
 Midstream, mining autonomous driving solution providers work closely with OEMs to
integrate autonomous driving systems into vehicle platforms through joint development
and system customization. These collaborations typically involve tailoring autonomous
capabilities to the specific requirements of mining environments. OEMs support
large-scale manufacturing and validation testing, while mining autonomous driving
solution providers lead software integration, sensor calibration, and system
optimization. Together, the two parties co-develop standardized autonomous mining
trucks capable of scaled deployment.
 Downstream, mining companies or general contractors purchase autonomous mining
trucksanddeploytheminoperations.Theirreal-worldfeedback,includingperformance,
safety,andutilizationdata,helpsdriveongoingiterationandimprovementofthemining
autonomous driving systems.
Mining autonomous driving solution providers occupy a critical position in the mining
automation ecosystem. They sit at the intersection of software, hardware, and operational
deployment, playing a central role in turning advanced driving technology into scalable, real-world
applications. In addition to developing the core autonomous driving stack, including perception,
path planning, and system safety, these companies are responsible for adapting the technology to
the unique demands of mining environments. Their close collaboration with OEMs, mining
operators, and infrastructure providers enables faster product development, tighter system
integration, and broader industry adoption. As the link between upstream innovation and
downstream deployment, mining autonomous driving solution providers are key to unlocking
commercial autonomous driving at scale.
Market Size for Mining Autonomous Driving Solutions in China
Autonomous mining is approaching a critical inflection point in China. As the broader
automotive industry transitions from electrification to automation, purpose-built autonomous
driving vehicles are gaining traction in industrial settings where safety, efficiency, and cost
reduction are high priorities. Mining, in particular, stands out as one of the most promising early
markets for scaled commercial deployment.
Adoption of autonomous mining trucks is expected to accelerate meaningfully over the next
five years. Penetration is projected to reach more than 50% by 2030. Increasing regulatory support,
continuous technological advancements, and the inherent suitability of the mining environment
collectively drive the rapid growth in the sales penetration rate of autonomous mining truck in
China. On the one hand, the Guidelines for High-Quality Development of Open-Pit Coal Mines
(《露天煤礦高質量發展指導意見》) issued by China National Coal Association explicitly strongly
drive industry transformation by encouraging 80% of open-pit coal mining capacity to achieve
intelligentization by 2030. On the other hand, the maturing autonomous driving technology has
reduced hardware costs and enhanced software standardization, improving the solution’s cost-
effectiveness and scalability. Simultaneously, the inherently enclosed and controlled nature of
miningsitesmakesautonomousdrivingmoreviableinminesthaninurbanorhighwaysettings.The
synergy of these factors provides a solid foundation for the sustained future growth of autonomous
mining truck adoption in China. To put this in perspective, the sales of autonomous mining trucks
inChinaareexpectedtogrowfromover4,500unitsin2026toapproximately15,000unitsby2030,
representing a CAGR of 34.4%. This trajectory mirrors the rapid rise of new energy vehicles

(NEVs) in China, where sales surged once penetration crossed the 10% threshold. Given the
operational and economic incentives, autonomous driving in mining may scale even faster than
NEVs did, following a similar but steeper adoption curve.

In the mining autonomous driving solution industry, there are two business models: the
Company-provided fleet model and the customer-provided fleet model. Under the Company-
provided fleet model, mining autonomous driving solution providers possess and manage the fleet
of autonomous mining trucks, offering comprehensive services that integrate vehicles, operational
management, and technical support as a complete solution. This model allows customers to deploy
autonomousdrivingsystemswithoutpurchasingtrucks,makingitidealforcustomersseekingrapid
implementation,reducedupfrontinvestment,andmanagedoperations.Underthismodel,customers
typically make recurring payments. Fees are generally tied to the volume of material transported,
with pricing commonly calculated on a per-cubic-meter or per-tonne basis. The specific rates vary
across different mining sites, depending on factors such as haul distance, slope conditions, and
overall site complexity. Conversely, under the customer-provided fleet model, the customers
procureandowntheirownautonomousminingtrucksequippedwithautonomousdrivingsolutions,
while the service providers provide customers with operation-related services, such as software
updates, platform maintenance and remote driving assistance. The customer-provided fleet model
is designed for customers that already have established operating teams, require tailored solutions,
or prioritize long-term cost efficiency. Under this model, mining companies or contractors either
make a one-time purchase of autonomous mining trucks or obtain them through leasing
arrangements with truck and equipment holding companies. In addition, service providers may
charge usage-based service fees on top of the truck purchase price that are typically linked to the
volume of material transported, with pricing commonly calculated on a per-cubic-meter basis. The
applicable rates may vary across different mining deployments based on factors such as haul
distance, slope conditions, and overall site complexity. In parallel, service providers have
introduced two alternative pricing models: a predetermined per-truck fee based on the number of
trucks deployed, with rates varying by project, and a one-time fee for the entire deployment. These
two models demonstrate the flexibility of mining autonomous driving solutions in asset allocation
andservicedepth,addressingdiversecustomerneedsincostmanagement,operationalcapacity,and
system integration. In 2025, the proportions of market size in terms of revenue for China’s mining
autonomous driving solution industry under Company-provided fleet model and customer-provided
fleet model are 26.3% and 73.7%, respectively.
AutonomousminingtrucksinChinaareprimarilycategorizedintofourtypes:range-extended
wide-body trucks, battery-electric wide-body trucks, diesel wide-body trucks and rigid-frame
mining trucks, which accounted for approximately 54.8%, 18.5%, 15.9% and 10.8% of the total
number of autonomous mining trucks in China as of 2025 respectively. Wide-body trucks typically
operate in the sub-100-tonnage payload range, while rigid trucks generally exceed 100 tonnes in
capacity. Among these, range-extended wide-body trucks have become the mainstream choice for
autonomous deployment in open-pit mines, due to their flexible refueling options, adaptability
across diverse mining environment, and cost-effectiveness.
Payload capacity across the sector ranges from approximately 45 tonnes to 330 tonnes. The
100-tonnage class has emerged as the core platform for China’s intelligent mining transformation.
These vehicles combine automation, electrification, large-scale design, and domestic
manufacturing. Compared to smaller models, 100-tonnage autonomous mining trucks offer
– 73 –

significantly higher throughput and lower cost-per-tonne-mile, making them well-suited for
high-volume, large-site operations. In 2025, 100-tonnage class vehicles represented around 50% of
all autonomous mining trucks in China by payload segment.
Key Drivers of the Mining Autonomous Driving Solution Industry in China
Severalstructuralandpolicytrendsareacceleratingthegrowthofminingautonomousdriving
solution industry in China:
Policy momentum is accelerating adoption at scale
In recent years, China has launched a number of initiatives at both the central and local levels
to advance intelligent mining, autonomous driving technologies, and low-carbon development as
well as to accelerate the deployment of autonomous driving solutions in the mining sector, creating
a broad market space for mining autonomous driving solution providers.
At the national level, among the policy documents such as the “Guidelines for the Intelligent
Construction of Coal Mines” (《煤礦智能化建設指南》), the “Circular on Supporting the
Construction of a New Generation ofArtificial Intelligence DemonstrationApplication Scenarios”
(《關於支持建設新一代人工智能示範應用場景的通知》), and the “Circular on Further
Accelerating the Intelligent Construction of Coal Mines to Promote the High-Quality Development
of Coal” (《關於進一步加快煤礦智能化建設促進煤炭高質量發展的通知》), the Chinese
government has explicitly called for accelerating the application of autonomous technology in the
field of mine transportation and encouraging enterprises to promote autonomous mining trucks to
enhance safety and operational efficiency. InApril 2024, the National Mine SafetyAdministration
and the National Development and Reform Commission jointly issued the “Guiding Opinions on
Deeply Promoting the Intelligent Construction of Mines and Promoting the Safe Development of
Mines” (《關於深入推進礦山智能化建設促進礦山安全發展的指導意見》), which set clear targets:
by 2026, more than 30% of all coal mine working faces are expected to adopt intelligent systems,
of which at least 80% are anticipated to operate under regular autonomous conditions. In addition,
the policy requires that intelligent equipment or robotics replace at least 30% of high-risk roles in
coalminesand20%innon-coalmines.Furthermore,in2024,theMinistryofNaturalResourcesand
sixotherministriesjointlyreleasedtheCircularonFurtherStrengtheningtheConstructionofGreen
Mines (《關於進一步加強綠色礦山建設的通知》), which encourages the application of advanced
green and low-carbon technologies to accelerate the transformation toward sustainable mining.The
policy also calls for deeper integration of digital technologies, including 5G, big data, the Internet,
and artificial intelligence, to promote the intelligence and greening of mining, thereby improving
resource utilization efficiency and production management capabilities. These beneficial policies
will further boost the growth of the mining autonomous driving solution industry in China.
Meanwhile, local governments have also helped mining enterprises adopt mining autonomous
driving solutions through financial subsidies, industrial support, and demonstration projects. For
instance, major coal mining provinces such as Xinjiang and Inner Mongolia have taken the lead in
laying out demonstration areas for autonomous mining trucks to promote large-scale application in
the industry. “Xinjiang’s 2023-2025ThreeYearAction Plan for Coal Mine Intelligence” (《新疆維
吾爾自治區煤礦智能化建設三年行動計劃(2023-2025年)》) clearly stipulates that different
intelligentoperationmodelsshouldbedevelopedbasedondifferentminingprocesstypes,including
the adoption of autonomous mining trucks to enhance the overall operational efficiency of the
mining areas. The General Office of the People’s Government of Inner Mongolia Autonomous
Region issued the “Notice on Several Measures to Further Strengthen the Safety Management of
Open-pit Coal Mines in the Region” (《內蒙古自治區人民政府關於進一步加強全區露天煤礦安全
管理若干措施的通知》), explicitly encouraging existing open-pit coal mines with large reserves,
strongon-sitemanagement,andwell-staffedtechnicalteamstopromotetheapplicationofadvanced
technologies such as autonomous driving and slope radar monitoring.The aim is to further enhance
safety production levels through intelligent and digital transformation.
AI is driving meaningful gains in automation and productivity
AI is fundamentally transforming autonomous mining truck operations in complex and
dynamic environments by enhancing perception, route planning, and decision-making through deep
learning and real-time data processing, thereby reducing accidents, lowering human intervention,
and enabling smarter dispatching and maintenance. More importantly,AI-driven rapid learning and
system iteration have become the key breakthrough, as exemplified by our Group’s proprietary
trainingenginebuiltonover100high-frequencyreal-minescenarios,whichhasshortenednew-site
deployment time from three months to 3 days.

Technology breakthroughs are solving long-standing industry bottlenecks
Insufficient performance of drive-by-wire electronic controlling chassis systems and
incompatibility between fault diagnostics and autonomous driving systems have been key
challenges hindering the deployment of autonomous mining trucks. Industry-leading companies
have achieved technological breakthroughs by developing proprietary drive-by-wire electronic
controlling chassis platforms. For example, our Group has developed drive-by-wire electronic
controlling platform for 100-tonnage autonomous mining trucks, deeply integrating vehicle control
with autonomous driving algorithms. This enables high-precision steering, braking, and power
distribution in complex operational scenarios, providing critical technical support for unmanned
haulage. The platform leverages a closed-loop data system and real-time self-diagnostic functions
to continuously optimize operational workflows, significantly reducing failure rates and enhancing
operational continuity. These breakthroughs have not only improved the autonomous decision-
making capabilities, safety, and reliability of autonomous mining trucks but also enhanced their
adaptability in complex conditions, laying a solid foundation for large-scale deployment of mining
autonomous driving solutions.
Growing mining output creates demand for autonomous driving systems
Driven by rising demand for mineral resources from downstream industries such as new
energy, power infrastructure and advanced manufacturing, China’s mining industry has continued
to expand its production capacity. China’s major non-ferrous metal production grew from 64.8
million tonnes in 2021 to 81.8 million tonnes in 2025, indicating sustained growth in mining
activities. As mining production activities continue to expand and transportation requirements
within mining sites increase, demand for autonomous driving solutions is expected to grow
accordingly, supporting the continued expansion of the mining autonomous driving solution
industry in China.
Trends in China’s Mining Autonomous Driving Solution Market
Key trends shaping the mining autonomous driving solution industry in China include:
Expansion beyond open-pit coal mines
Adoption of autonomous mining trucks is rapidly expanding beyond traditional open-pit coal
mines into metal mines, quarries, and other resource types. This trend is being driven by maturing
technology and growing commercial validation. As of the end of 2024, over 2,000 autonomous
miningtruckshadbeendeployedinChina’sopen-pitcoalmines,reflectingbroadrecognitionofthe
technology’s feasibility.
At the same time, demand is rising in metal mines (such as copper and iron) and quarries, as
autonomous driving systems become more adaptable to varying mining environment, workflows,
and safety conditions. This expansion is further supported by government-led smart mining
initiatives in China and other countries, which continue to prioritize automation in mine transport
operations, accelerating cross-segment adoption.
Chinese autonomous mining technology is going global
Although mining-rich regions such as Australia and Chile are well suited for autonomous
deployment, adoption has been constrained by high equipment and operating costs and limited
localized support from international vendors. In contrast, leading Chinese players benefit from
scale-driven cost advantages and closer integration with Chinese mining groups that are expanding
overseas,makinghomegrownautonomoussolutionsmoreattractiveduetobettercostcontrol,faster
service response, and lower deployment risk. This alignment between outbound mining investment
and autonomous technology export is forming a positive feedback loop, as overseas deployments
enhance Chinese players’ product iteration, localization capabilities, and global presence through
patents and strategic partnerships.

RISING GLOBAL DEMAND FOR MINING AUTONOMOUS DRIVING SOLUTION
Mining companies around the world are under pressure from two persistent challenges: labor
shortages and rising costs. In major resource regions like Australia, Canada and Chile, it is
becoming increasingly difficult — and expensive — to staff remote, high-risk operations. Manual
driving not only limits productivity but also introduces safety and cost risks that are hard to scale
away.
Autonomous mining trucks offer a compelling alternative. With the ability to operate 24/7,
followoptimizedroutes,andminimizefuelorpowerusage,thesesystemscansignificantlyimprove
efficiency while reducing total operating costs. As global mining expands into harder-to-access
reservesandtheindustryacceleratesitsenergytransition,automationisshiftingfromamereoption
to a strategic priority.
Governments worldwide are taking notice of this trend. In 2025, the Department of Mines in
Western Australia updated its formal Code of Practice for autonomous mining operations, setting
standards around system safety, monitoring, and operator training. This regulatory clarity is giving
mine operators the confidence to deploy autonomous driving at scale, pushing automation from
pilot stage into full commercial rollout. Driven by ESG initiatives, digital transformation, and the
growing demand for safer, more sustainable operations, autonomous driving is shifting from pilot
programs to large-scale deployment. The global market size in terms of revenue for mining
autonomous driving solutions is expected to grow from approximately US$1.0 billion in 2025 to
US$7.3 billion by 2030, representing a CAGR of approximately 47.4%. The market size in terms
ofrevenueforminingautonomousdrivingsolutionsinAustraliaisexpectedtoreachUS$2.9billion
in2030,reflectingthecountry’searlyadoptionandscaleadvantagesinminingautomation.Thesize
of global total addressable market for mining autonomous driving solutions is over US$110.0
billion. The global ownership penetration rate of autonomous mining truck is expected to increase
from approximately 5.5% in 2026 to 28.0% in 2030. As of 2025, rigid-frame mining trucks,
range-extended wide-body trucks, battery-electric wide-body trucks and diesel wide-body trucks
accounted for approximately 36.4%, 39.0%, 14.5% and 10.1% of the total number of global
autonomous mining trucks respectively.

while also delivering fully integrated, full-stack solutions rather than standalone products. In
addition, mining customers adopt new technologies cautiously, favoring vendors with strong track
records and domain expertise in mining operations. High upfront investment in vehicles, hardware,
software development and high capex related to self-owned fleets further limit new entrants,
reinforcing the industry’s concentrated and high-barrier competitive landscape.
Overview of Mining Digitalization Solution Market
Conventional mining operations are often hindered by outdated dispatching methods, low
operational efficiency, and persistent safety risks. Poor coordination across various tasks results in
frequent idle times and misaligned workflows. For instance, trucks may experience prolonged
waiting time for loading, while excavators sit idle due to delays in vehicle dispatch. In addition,
inefficient planning, such as poorly designed dumping site layouts, can lead to excessively long
transport distances, further driving up fuel consumption and labor costs. These inefficiencies,
combined with imbalanced resource allocation and rising operational expenditures, underscore the
urgent need for systemic transformation in how mines are managed and operated.
Mining digitalization solutions, underpinned by intelligent perception, integrated platforms,
and system-wide coordination, are reshaping the mining industry into a digital, automated, and
intelligent ecosystem. By leveraging advanced data analytics, IoT technologies, and real-time
monitoring, these solutions enhance core operational domains such as excavation, transportation,
and dumping. They also support the intelligent scheduling and digital management of both
autonomy sites and non-autonomy sites. Furthermore, mining digitalization platforms enable
real-time decision-making and streamline critical functions including production planning, safety
supervision, asset tracking, and field inspections. This end-to-end digital transformation not only
boosts efficiency and safety but also lays the foundation for sustainable and resilient mining
operations. The size of China’s mining digitalization solution market in terms of revenue was
RMB40.2 billion in 2025 and is expected to exceed RMB80.0 billion by 2030. In 2025, Our Group
accounted for approximately 0.01% of the mining digitalization solution market in China.
Leading mining autonomous driving solutions providers are now leveraging their expertise in
the transportation segment to provide mining digitalization solutions that optimize core production
workflows.Drawingonadvancedtechnologiessuchasdataanalytics,IoTintegration,andreal-time
monitoring, these providers are rolling out modular and scalable platforms that support both
conventional operations and mines progressing toward higher levels of automation. For instance,
some solution offers unified orchestration of manned and unmanned fleets, intelligent dispatching,
and integrated control of key mining equipment. By bridging fragmented systems and enabling
end-to-enddataflow,thesesolutionshelpminingcompaniesimproveoperationalefficiency,reduce
costs, and strengthen safety management, driving the industry’s transition toward digitalized,
resilient, and high-performance mining ecosystems.

REGULATIONS AND POLICIES RELATING TO PROMOTING THE SAFE
DEVELOPMENT AND THE INTELLIGENT CONSTRUCTION OF MINES
For ensuring safety in production in mines, preventing accidents and protecting personal
safety of workers and staff at mines, and promoting the development of mining industry, the Mine
Safety Law of the People’s Republic of China (《中華人民共和國礦山安全法》) (the “PRC Mine
Safety Law”) latest amended on August 27, 2009, stipulates that mining enterprises must possess
facilities that ensure safety in production, establish and perfect the system of safety management,
takeeffectivemeasurestoimprovetheworkingconditionsforworkersandstaff,andstrengthenthe
work of safety control in mines in order to ensure safe production. Besides, according to the
Regulations for the Implementation of the PRC Mine Safety Law (《中華人民共和國礦山安全法實
施條例》), promulgated by the Ministry of Labor on October 30, 1996, the equipment (including
butnotlimitedtoequipmentforcontaining/conveying,transport),apparatus,protectivearticlesand
safetydetectinginstrumentsshallconformtonationalsafetystandardsorthetradesafetystandards;
those which do not may be used.
OnAugust9,2023,inordertostrengthenthetop-leveldesignofintelligentmineconstruction,
the National Mine Safety Administration formulated the Intelligent Mine Standardization
Framework (《礦山智能化標準體系框架》), which systematically identifies standardization needs
across mining sectors, pioneering integration of coal and non-coal mine standards under a unified
system, and defines specific R&D priorities for intelligent mine components.
OnApril 24, 2024, for further promoting the intelligent construction of mines, and promoting
the safe development of mines, the National Mine Safety Administration, the Ministry of
Emergency Management, the National Development and Reform Commission (“NDRC”), the
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the Ministry of Science and Technology, the
Ministry of Finance and the Ministry of Education issued the Notice by of Issuing the Guiding
Opinions on Further Advancing the Intelligent Construction of Mines and Promoting the Safe
Development of Mines (《國家礦山安監局、應急管理部、國家發展改革委、工業和信息化部、科
技部、財政部、教育部關於印發<關於深入推進礦山智能化建設促進礦山安全發展的指導意見>的
通知》), stating that by 2030, a complete intelligent mining system will be established to realize
deep integration and shared application of mining data, mining operation with less people and
without people will be promoted, major safety risks shall be effectively prevented and controlled,
and the essential safety level of mines will be significantly improved. The research and
development of “containment” technologies that restrict intelligent construction shall be
accelerated. Key technologies such as transparent geology, unmanned driving under complex
conditions, collaborative control of intelligent equipment cluster, and industrial software shall be
tackled. The integration and application of new technologies such as 5G, industrial Internet, big
data, cloud computing, artificial intelligence, and digital twin with traditional mining shall be
promoted. The research and development and application of core components, sensors, key control
units, and operating systems of intelligent equipment of mines shall be accelerated, and the
development and iterative updating of mine robots shall be accelerated. High-end mining sensors
and special instruments and equipment shall be developed. The research and development and
application of intelligent core equipment such as intelligent shovel loading and transportation
equipment, new mining unmanned vehicles shall be strengthened.
On May 21, 2024, National EnergyAdministration Notice on FurtherAccelerating Intelligent
Coal Mine Construction to Promote High-Quality Development of the Coal Industry (《國家能源
局關於進一步加快煤礦智能化建設促進煤炭高質量發展的通知》) was promulgated by National
Energy Administration. To implement the decisions of the CPC Central Committee and the State
Council on developing new quality productive forces and integrating digital intelligence
technologies with the coal industry, the notice outlines measures to accelerate intelligent coal mine
constructionandpromotehigh-qualitydevelopment.Foropen-pitcoalmines,thenoticeemphasizes
enhancingintelligentmulti-processcoordinationcapabilitiesandfocusesonadvancingautonomous
excavation and loading, unmanned driving of mining trucks, robotic collaboration in loading-
transportation-dumping workflows, and encourages to implement truck platooning for unmanned
haulage.

REGULATIONS AND POLICIES RELATING TO THE AUTONOMOUS DRIVING
INDUSTRY
According to the Taxonomy of Driving Automation for Vehicles (《汽車駕駛自動化分級》)
which was promulgated by the StateAdministration for Market Regulation (the “SAMR”) and the
National Standardization Administration on August 20, 2021 and became effective on March 1,
2022, the standards for autonomous driving can be divided into: L0 (emergency assistance), L1
(partial driver assistance), L2 (combined driver assistance), L3 (conditionally automated driving),
L4 (highly automated driving) and L5 (fully automated driving).
According to the Strategies for the Innovative Development of IntelligentVehicles (《智能汽
車創新發展戰略》) which was promulgated by the NDRC, the Office of the Central Leading Group
for CyberspaceAffairs, the Ministry of Science and Technology of the People’s Republic of China
(the “MOST”) and other eight ministries and commissions, China’s standard intelligent vehicle
system will be fully established and more complete from 2035 to 2050. The vision of a safe,
efficient,greenandcivilizedpowerofintelligentvehicleswillbegraduallyrealized,andintelligent
vehicles will fully meet the people’s growing needs for a better life.
In January 2022, the Ministry of Transport and the MOST jointly issued the Outline for the
Mid- to Long-Term Development of Technological Innovation in the Transportation
Sector (2021−2035) (《交通領域科技創新中長期發展規劃綱要(2021−2035年)》) outlining
initiatives to promote the development and large-scale application of autonomous driving
technology.
In addition, the Guidelines on Transportation Safety Services for Autonomous Vehicles (for
Trial Implementation) (《自動駕駛汽車運輸安全服務指南(試行)》) issued by the Ministry of
Transport on November 21, 2023, provides relevant guidance for vehicles which are capable of
performing all dynamic driving tasks under designed operating conditions according to relevant
national standards and have obtained the access approvals from the MIIT, including but not limited
to, requirements for application scenarios, operators of autonomous vehicles, safety and security,
supervision and overall management.
REGULATIONS ON PRC CORPORATION
The establishment, operation and management of corporate entities in the PRC are governed
by the Company Law of the People’s Republic of China (the “PRC Company Law”), which was
promulgated by the Standing Committee of the NPC (the “SCNPC”) in December 1993 and latest
amended in December 2023, according to which, PRC companies are generally classified into
limited liability companies and joint stock limited companies.The PRC Company Law also applies
to foreign-invested limited liability companies and companies limited by shares. According to the
PRC Company Law, where laws on foreign investment have other stipulations, such stipulations
shall prevail.
REGULATIONS ON FOREIGN INVESTMENT AND OVERSEAS INVESTMENT
Regulations on Foreign Investment
Investment in the PRC by foreign investors is mainly regulated by the Catalogue of
Encourages Industries for Foreign Investment (2025 Edition) (《鼓勵外商投資產業目錄》(2025年
版)), which was promulgated by the Ministry of Commerce of the PRC (the “MOFCOM”) and the
NDRC on December 15, 2025 and took effect on February 1, 2026, and the SpecialAdministrative
Measures for Access of Foreign Investment (2024 Edition) (《外商投資准入特別管理措施(負面清
單)》(2024年版)) (the “Negative List”), which was promulgated by the MOFCOM and the NDRC
on September 6, 2024 and took effect on November 1, 2024. The Negative List sets out several
restrictive measures in a unified manner, such as the requirements on shareholding percentages and
management for the access of foreign investments in the industries listed in the Negative List and
the industries that are prohibited from foreign investment.Any industries not listed in the Negative
List shall be administered under the principle of equal treatment to domestic and foreign
investment. The industry of smart sensing interaction R&D, production and operation is not listed
in the Negative List, which means the foreign investment in the business operated by us in the PRC
shall not be restricted or prohibited.
On March 15, 2019, the NPC promulgated the Foreign Investment Law (《中華人民共和國外

Regulations on Overseas Investment
Pursuant to the Measures for the Administration of Overseas Investment (《境外投資管理辦

Pursuant to the Measures for theAdministration of Overseas Investment of Enterprises (《企

Edition) (《境外投資敏感行業目錄(2018年版)》) issued by the NDRC on January 31, 2018 and
came into effect on March 1, 2018 lists the sensitive industries in detail.

Regulations on Product Quality
The principal legal provisions governing product liability are set out in the Product Quality
Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國產品質量法》) (the “Product Quality Law”), which took
effectonSeptember1,1993andwaslastamendedonDecember29,2018.ViolationsoftheProduct
Quality Law may result in the imposition of fines. In addition, the relevant seller or producer will
beorderedtosuspenditsoperationsanditsbusinesslicensewillberevoked.Criminalliabilitymay
be incurred in serious cases.
According to the Product Quality Law and the Civil Code of the PRC (《中華人民共和國民
法典》) (the “Civil Code”), which was promulgated by the NPC on May 28, 2020 and took effect
on January 1, 2021, if defects are found after the product is put into circulation, producers and
sellersshallpromptlytakeremedialmeasuressuchasstoppingsales,issuingwarningsandrecalling
the product. If the party fails to take remedial measures in time or fails to take effective remedial
measures and results in increased damage thereof, it shall also bear tortious liability for the
increased damage. When recall measures are taken in accordance with the above-mentioned
stipulations, the producers or sellers shall bear the necessary expenses incurred to the infringed.
When a product is manufactured or sold with full knowledge of its defects, or the person in charge
fails to take effective remedial measures in accordance with the above-mentioned stipulations,
which cause death or serious damage to the health of others, the infringed party shall have the right
to claim appropriate punitive damage.
Regulations on Employment
ThemajorPRClawsandregulationsthatgovernemploymentrelationshipsaretheLaborLaw
of the PRC (《中華人民共和國勞動法》), which was released by the SCNPC on July 5, 1994 and
latest amended on December 29, 2018, and the Labor Contract Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和
國勞動合同法》) (the “Labor Contract Law”), which was released by the SCNPC on June 29,
2007 and latest amended on December 28, 2012. These laws and their implementation regulations
impose stringent requirements on the employers in relation to entering into fixed-term employment
contracts, hiring of temporary employees and dismissal of employees.
Pursuant to the Labor Contract Law, labor contracts must be executed in writing if labor
relationships are to be or have been established between employers and employees, the principles
of lawfulness, fairness, equality, free will, negotiation for agreement and good faith shall be
observed in the formation of a labor contract. An employer shall establish a sound system of
employment rules in accordance with the laws to ensure that its employees enjoy the labor rights
and perform the employment obligations.
Regulations on Social Insurance and Housing Accumulation Funds
As required under the Social Insurance Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國社會保險法》)
which was released by the SCNPC on October 28, 2010, came into force on July 1, 2011 and was
then amended on December 29, 2018 and the Interim Regulations Concerning the Collection and
Payment of Social Insurance Premiums (《社會保險費徵繳暫行條例》) amended by the State
CouncilandmadeeffectiveonMarch24,2019,enterprisesareobligedtocarryoutsocialinsurance
registration at the local social insurance agency and provide their employees in the PRC with
welfare schemes covering basic pension insurance, unemployment insurance, maternity insurance,
work-relatedinjuryinsuranceandbasicmedicalinsurance.Thesepaymentsaremadetolocalsocial
insurance collection administrative authorities and any employer that fails to contribute may be
fined and ordered to make up within a prescribed time limit.
On July 31, 2025, the PRC Supreme People’s Court promulgated the Supreme People’s
Court’s Interpretation (II) on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Labor Dispute
Cases (《最高人民法院關於審理勞動爭議案件適用法律問題的解釋(二)》) (the “New Judicial
Interpretation”), which took effect on September 1, 2025.According to theArticle 19 of the New
JudicialInterpretation,ifanemployerandanemployeeagreeortheemployeeundertakesthatsocial
insurance contributions need not to be paid, the court shall deem such agreement or undertaking
invalid.
Pursuant to the Regulation on theAdministration of HousingAccumulation Funds (《住房公
積金管理條例》) released by the State Council on April 3, 1999 and effective as of the same day,
which was latest amended by the State Council and came into effect on March 24, 2019, an
employer shall undergo the formalities for contribution registration of housing accumulation fund
with the housing accumulation fund management center, and undergo the formalities for opening
housing provident fund accounts to pay the housing accumulation funds for its employees in
accordance with the relevant provisions of the state.

Regulations on Production Safety
Pursuant to the Production Safety Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國安全生產法》) which
was latest amended by the SCNPC on June 10, 2021, production and operation entities shall abide
by the Production Safety Law of the PRC and other laws and regulations concerning work safety,
and redouble their efforts to ensure work safety by setting up and perfecting the responsibility
system for work safety of all employees and rules and regulations on work safety, increasing the
input and guarantee of funds, materials, technologies and personnel in terms of work safety,
improving the conditions for work safety, strengthening the development of standards and adoption
ofinformationtechnologiesforworksafety,buildingadualpreventionmechanismoflevel-to-level
safety risk management and control and hidden danger identification and management, and
perfecting the risk prevention and resolution mechanism, to raise the work safety level and ensure
work safety.
Regulations on Fire Prevention
According to the Fire Prevention Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國消防法》) promulgated
by SCNPC onApril 29, 1998, last amended onApril 29, 2021 and made effective on the same day,
the Emergency Management Authority of the State Council and its local counterparts at or above
the county level shall monitor and administer the fire prevention affairs, and the fire prevention
design or construction of a construction project must conform to the national fire prevention
technical standards for engineering construction. According to the Interim Provisions on the
Administration of Fire Protection Design Review and Final Inspection of Construction Projects
(《建設工程消防設計審查驗收管理暫行規定》), promulgated by the Ministry of Housing and
Urban-Rural Development on April 1, 2020, last amended on August 21, 2023 and officially
implemented on October 30, 2023, special construction projects as defined under the Interim
Provisions shall conduct fire protection design review and fire protection acceptance inspection,
construction projects other than such special construction projects shall file protection acceptance
of the project with competent authority.
REGULATIONS ON INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS
Regulations on Trademarks
Trademarks are protected by the PRC Trademark Law (《中華人民共和國商標法》)
promulgated by the SCNPC onAugust 23, 1982, latest amended onApril 23, 2019 and effective on
November 1, 2019, as well as the Implementation Regulations of the PRC Trademark Law (《中華
人民共和國商標法實施條例》) promulgated by the State Council on August 3, 2002 and amended
on April 29, 2014, pursuant to which, the Trademark Office of National Intellectual Property
Administration, or the Trademark Office, is responsible for trademark registrations and
administration, and grants a term of ten years to registered trademarks and another ten years if
requested upon expiry of the first or any renewed ten-year term.
Regulations on Patents
According to the PRC Patent Law (《中華人民共和國專利法》) latest amended by the
SCNPC on October 17, 2020 and became effective on June 1, 2021, as well as the Detailed Rules
for the Implementation of the PRC Patent Law (《中華人民共和國專利法實施細則》) latest
amended by the State Council on December 11, 2023 and made effective on January 20, 2024, the
National Intellectual Property Administration, along with departments within provincial,
autonomous regions and municipalities governments that are in charge of patent administration, are
the responsible regulatory bodies for administering patents in the PRC. The PRC Patent Law and
its implementation rules provide for three types of patents, “invention”, “utility model” and
“design”, the duration of “invention”, “utility model” and “design” is separately twenty years, ten
years and fifteen years, commencing from the date of application.
Regulations on Copyrights
Pursuant to the PRC Copyright Law (《中華人民共和國著作權法》) which was latest
amended by the SCNPC on November 11, 2020 and took effect on June 1, 2021 and the
Implementing Regulations of the PRC Copyright Law (《中華人民共和國著作權法實施條例》)
whichwaslatestamendedbytheStateCouncilonJanuary30,2013andbecameeffectiveonMarch
1, 2013, the PRC citizens, legal persons, and other organizations shall, enjoy copyright in their
works, whether published or not, which include, among others, works of literature, art, and
scientific intellectual achievements that are original and capable of being reproduced in tangible
form. The copyright owner enjoys various kinds of rights, including the right of publication, the
right of authorship and the right of reproduction, etc..

Regulations on Design of Integrated Circuit Layouts
In order to protect the proprietary rights of integrated circuit layout designs, encourage
innovation in integrated circuit technology, and promote the development of science and
technology, the State Council promulgated the Regulations on the Protection of Integrated Circuit
Layout Designs (《集成電路佈圖設計保護條例》) (the “Regulations on the Protection”) onApril
2, 2001, which regulates that the owner of an integrated circuit layout design has exclusive rights
to the design, so long as they comply with the provisions of the Regulations on the Protection. The
exclusive rights to the layout design arise upon registration with the intellectual property
administrationdepartmentoftheStateCouncil,andlayoutdesignsthathavenotbeenregisteredare
not protected by the Regulations on the Protection. The protection period for the exclusive rights
of a layout design is 10 years, starting from the date of application for registration of the design or
from the date of putting it into commercial exploitation somewhere in the world for the first time,
whichever is earlier. However, whether or not the design is registered or commercially used, it is
no longer protected by the Regulations on the Protection 15 years after the date of completion of
the design.
REGULATIONS ON TAXATION
Principal Taxation of Our Company in the PRC
Enterprise Income Tax
Pursuant to the PRC Enterprise Income Tax Law (《中華人民共和國企業所得稅法》) (the
“EIT Law”), promulgated by the SCNPC on March 16, 2007, latest amended and effective on
December 29, 2018, and the Implementation Regulations of the Enterprise Income Tax Law of the
PRC (《中華人民共和國企業所得稅法實施條例》) (the “EITIR”) promulgated by the State
Council on December 6, 2007, latest amended on December 6, 2024 and effective as of January 20,
2025, the enterprise income tax of both domestic and foreign-invested enterprises is unified at 25%
with certain exceptions. Enterprises are classified as “resident enterprises” and “non-resident
enterprises”, resident enterprises typically pay an enterprise income tax at the rate of 25%.
TheAdministrative Measures for Determination of High-tech Enterprises (《高新技術企業認
定管理辦法》), issued by the MOST, the MOF and the SATonApril 14, 2008, became effective on
January1,2008,andwasamendedonJanuary29,2016andtookeffectonJanuary1,2016.TheEIT
Law set out the sort of enterprises that are capable of enjoying tax reduction. Pursuant to the
Circular of the State Administration of Taxation on the Issues Concerning Implementation of the
PreferentialIncomeTaxPolicyforNewHigh-TechEnterprises(《國家稅務總局關於實施高新技術
企業所得稅優惠政策有關問題的公告》) issued on June 19, 2017 and made effective on the same
day, the enterprise income tax rate of new high-tech enterprises requiring national major support
should be reduced to 15%.

Value-added Tax
Pursuant to the Value-Added Tax Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國增值稅法》) (the “VAT
Law”) promulgated by the SCNPC on December 25, 2024 and effective on January 1, 2026, all

by taxpayers.
Taxation of Security Holders in the PRC
Taxation on Dividends
— the Individual Investor
Pursuant to the Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國個人所得稅法》)
(the “IIT Law”), latest amended on August 31, 2018 and effective as of January 1, 2019 and the
Implementation Provisions of the Individual Income Tax Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國個人
所得稅法實施條例》), latest amended on December 18, 2018 and effective as of January 1, 2019,
dividends distributed by PRC enterprises are subject to individual income tax levied at a flat rate
of 20%. For a foreign individual who is not a resident of the PRC, the receipt of dividends from
an enterprise in the PRC is normally subject to individual income tax of 20% unless specifically
exempted by the tax authority of the State Council or reduced by relevant tax treaty.
In the meanwhile, according to the Notice on Issues Concerning Differentiated Individual
Income Tax Policies on Dividends and Bonus of Listed Companies (《關於上市公司股息紅利差別
化個人所得稅政策有關問題的通知》) which was issued by the Ministry of Finance, the SAT and
the CSRC on September 7, 2015 and came into effect on September 8, 2015, where an individual
holds more than one year of the shares of a listed company obtained from the public offering and
transfer of the stock market of the listed company, the dividend and bonus income shall be
temporarily exempted from individual income tax. Where an individual acquires shares of a listed
company from the public offering and transfer of the stock market by the listed company, if the
holdingperiodiswithinonemonth(inclusive),thedividendincomeshallbeincludedinthetaxable
income in full; if the holding period is more than one month but less than one year (inclusive), the
dividend income shall be included in the taxable income at the rate of 50%; the aforesaid income
shall be subject to individual income tax at a uniform rate of 20%.

Taxation on Income from Share Transfer
— the Individual Investor
Under the IIT Law and its implementation rules, individuals are subject to individual income

Pursuant to the Circular on Continuing the Temporary Exemption of Individual Income Tax on

or eliminated under applicable tax treaties or arrangements.
REGULATIONS ON FOREIGN EXCHANGE
Foreign exchange regulations in the PRC are primarily governed by theAdministration Rules
on the Foreign Exchange of the PRC (《外匯管理條例》) (the “Exchange Rules”) promulgated by
the State Council on January 29, 1996, latest amended and became effective on August 5, 2008
Under the Exchange Rules, the Renminbi is freely convertible for current account items, including
the distribution of dividends, interest and royalty payments, trade and service-related foreign
exchange transactions provided that the transaction is true and legitimate. Conversion of Renminbi
for capital account items, such as direct investments, loans, security investments and repatriations
of investment, however, is still subject to the approval or registration regulation of the State
Administration of Foreign Exchange (the “SAFE”).
The Decisions of Matters including Canceling and Adjusting a Batch of Administrative
Approval Items (《關於取消和調整一批行政審批項目等事項的決定》) promulgated by the State
council on October 23, 2014 canceled the approval requirement of the SAFE and its branches for
the remittance and settlement of the proceeds raised from the overseas listing of the foreign shares.
Pursuant to the Notice on Issues Concerning the Foreign Exchange Administration of
Overseas Listing (《關於境外上市外匯管理有關問題的通知》, the “SAFE Circular 54”)
promulgated by the SAFE on December 26, 2014, a domestic company shall, within 15 business
days from completion of its overseas listing issuance, register the overseas listing with the SAFE’s
localbranchattheplaceofitsincorporation.Theproceedsofadomesticcompanyfromanoverseas
listing may be remitted to a domestic account or deposited overseas, and the use of the proceeds
must be consistent with the content of the prospectus and other disclosure documents.
On December 24, 2025, the People’s bank of China and the SAFE promulgated the Notice on
Issues Concerning theAdministration of Proceeds Raised by Domestic Enterprises Listed Overseas
(《關於境內企業境外上市資金管理有關問題的通知》, the “Notice on Proceeds”) to further
facilitate efficient overseas financing for domestic enterprises, which will be effective on April 1,
2026 and replace the SAFE Circular 54. The Notice on Proceed specifies that funds raised from
overseas listings, as well as gains from share reductions or transfers, may be repatriated in either
foreign currency or Renminbi. For companies participating in H-share “full circulation” program,
dividends payable to domestic shareholders by the listed entity must be distributed in Renminbi
within China. Foreign currency proceeds repatriated from overseas listings may be settled
independently for domestic use, and listed companies are permitted to independently manage
exchange rate risks within China. In addition, the Notice on Proceeds standardizes the use of
proceeds by stipulating that proceeds from overseas listings and gains from share reductions or
– 86 –

=== PAGE 96 ===
