transfers should, in principle, be repatriated. Any surplus funds remitted overseas by shareholders
for share purchases, as well as funds arising from unsuccessful transactions, must be promptly
returned to China. Enterprises that meet specific conditions are allowed to retain raised proceeds
overseas for use.
On February 13, 2015, the SAFE promulgated the Notice of the State Administration of
Foreign Exchange on Further Simplifying and Improving the Foreign Exchange Administration
Policies on Direct Investments (《國家外匯管理局關於進一步簡化和改進直接投資外匯管理政策

On March 30, 2015, the SAFE issued the Circular of the State Administration of Foreign

Capital of Foreign-invested Enterprises (《國家外匯管理局關於改革外商投資企業外匯資本金結匯
管理方式的通知》)(the“SAFECircular19”),whichtookeffectandreplacedpreviousregulations
from June 1, 2015. Pursuant to the SAFE Circular 19, up to 100% of foreign currency capital of a
foreign-invested enterprise may be converted into RMB capital according to the actual operation of
the enterprise within the business scope at its will and the RMB capital converted from foreign
currency registered capital of a foreign-invested enterprise may be used for equity investments
within the PRC provided that such usage shall fall into the business scope of the foreign-invested
enterprise, which will be regarded as the reinvestment of foreign-invested enterprise.Although the
SAFE Circular 19 allows for the use of RMB converted from the foreign currency-denominated
capital for equity investments in the PRC, the restrictions continue to apply as to foreign-invested
enterprises’ use of the converted RMB for purposes beyond the business scope, for securities
investments,forRMBentrustedloansorforinter-companyRMBloans.OnJune9,2016,theSAFE
promulgated the Notice of the State Administration of Foreign Exchange on Reforming and
Standardizing the Foreign Exchange Settlement Management Policy of CapitalAccount (《國家外
匯管理局關於改革和規範資本項目結匯管理政策的通知》) (the “SAFE Circular 16”), which
reiterates some of the rules set forth in Circular 19, but changes the prohibition against using RMB
capital converted from foreign currency denominated registered capital of a foreign-invested
company to issue RMB entrusted loans to a prohibition against using such capital to issue loans to
non-affiliated enterprises, excluding those explicitly permitted within the business scope.
In addition, SAFE promulgated the Circular Regarding Further Promotion of the Facilitation
of Cross-Border Trade and Investment (《關於進一步促進跨境貿易投資便利化的通知》) (the
“SAFE Circular 28”) on October 23, 2019, which expressly allows foreign-invested enterprises
that do not have equity investments in their approved business scope to use their capital obtained
fromforeignexchangesettlementtomakedomesticequityinvestmentsaslongasthereisatruthful
investment and such investment is in compliance with the foreign investment-related laws and

On April 10, 2020, the SAFE promulgated Notice of the State Administration of Foreign
Exchange on Optimizing Foreign Exchange Administration to Support the Development of

REGULATIONS ON SECURITIES AND OVERSEAS LISTING
The Securities Law of the People’s Republic of China (《中華人民共和國證券法》) (the
“PRCSecuritiesLaw”)tookeffectonJuly1,1999andwasrevisedasofAugust28,2004,October
27,2005,June29,2013,August31,2014andDecember28,2019,respectively.ThePRCSecurities
Law, which was revised on December 28, 2019 and came into effect on March 1, 2020, is divided
into14chaptersand226articles,regulating,amongotherthings,theissueandtradingofsecurities,
the listing of securities, and takeovers of listed companies.Article 224 of the PRC Securities Law
provides those domestic enterprises which, directly or indirectly, issue securities or list and trade
their securities outside the PRC shall comply with the relevant regulations of the State Council.
Currently, the issue and trading of foreign-issued securities (including shares) are principally
governed by the regulations and rules promulgated by the State Council and the CSRC. The CSRC
is the securities regulatory body set up by the State Council to supervise and administer the
securities market according to law, maintain order in the market, and ensure the market operates in
a lawful manner. Currently, the issue and trading of H shares are principally governed by the
regulations and rules promulgated by the State Council and the CSRC.
On February 17, 2023, the CSRC promulgated theTrialAdministrative Measures of Overseas
SecuritiesOfferingandListingbyDomesticCompanies(《境內企業境外發行證券和上市管理試行
辦法》)(the“TrialMeasures”)alongwithseveralapplicableguidance,whichbecameeffectiveon
March 31, 2023.
Pursuant to the Trial Measures, PRC domestic enterprises which seek to issue and list
securities in overseas markets by direct or indirect means are required to complete the filing
procedures with and submit relevant materials to the CSRC. The CSRC and competent authorities
under the State Council shall, to the extent of their respective mandate and according to law,
exercise supervision and regulation over domestic companies that offer and list securities in
overseas markets, and securities companies and securities service providers that provide domestic
services to such activities.
Where a domestic company fails to fulfill the filing procedures, or if there are conditions that
prohibit the overseas offering and listing by such domestic enterprise, and the enterprise proceeds
with overseas offering and listing, such company may be subject to order to rectify, warnings and
fines, and its controlling shareholders, actual controllers, the person directly in charge and other
directly responsible persons may also be subject to fines. No overseas offering and listing shall be
made under any of the following circumstances: (i) where such securities offering and listing is
explicitly prohibited by provisions in laws, administrative regulations and relevant state rules; (ii)
where the intended securities offering and listing may endanger national security as reviewed and
determinedbycompetentauthoritiesundertheStateCouncilinaccordancewithlaw;(iii)wherethe
domestic company intending to make the securities offering and listing, or its controlling
shareholders and the actual controller, have committed crimes such as corruption, bribery,
embezzlement, misappropriation of property or undermining the order of the socialist market
economy during the latest three years; (iv) where the domestic company intending to make the
securities offering and listing is suspected of committing crimes or major violations of laws and
regulations, and is under investigation according to law, and no conclusion has yet been made
thereof; and (v) where there are material ownership disputes over equity held by the domestic
company’s controlling shareholder or by other shareholders that are controlled by the controlling
shareholder and/or actual controller.
On February 24, 2023, the CSRC, the MOF, the National Administration of State Secrets
Protection and the National Archives Administration of China jointly issued the Provisions on
Strengthening the Confidentiality and Archives Administration Related to the Overseas Securities
Offering and Listing by Domestic Enterprises (《關於加強境內企業境外發行證券和上市相關保密
和檔案管理工作的規定》), which took effect on March 31, 2023, according to which, overseas
securities regulators and competent overseas authorities may request to inspect, investigate or
collect evidence from a domestic company concerning its overseas offering and listing or from the
domestic securities companies and securities service providers that undertake relevant businesses
for such domestic companies, such inspection, investigation and evidence collection shall be
conducted under a cross-border regulatory cooperation mechanism, and the CSRC or other
competent Chinese authorities will provide necessary assistance pursuant to bilateral and
multilateral cooperation mechanisms. The domestic company, securities companies and securities
service providers shall first obtain approval from the CSRC or other competent Chinese authorities
– 88 –

=== PAGE 98 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
before cooperating with the inspection and investigation by the overseas securities regulator or
competent overseas authority, or providing documents and materials requested in such inspection
and investigation. To be specific, a domestic company that plans to, either directly or through its
overseas listed entity, publicly disclose or provide to relevant individuals or entities including
securities companies, securities service providers and overseas regulators, (i) any documents and
materials that contain state secrets or working secrets of government agencies, shall first obtain
approvalfromcompetentauthoritiesandfilewithcompetentsecrecyadministrativedepartment;(ii)

REGULATIONS RELATED TO THE “FULL CIRCULATION” OF H SHARE
“Full circulation” means listing and circulating on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange of the
domestic unlisted shares of an H-share listed company, including unlisted domestic shares held by
domestic shareholders prior to overseas listing, unlisted domestic shares additionally issued after
overseas listing, and unlisted shares held by foreign shareholders, which was mainly regulated by
the Guidelines for the “Full Circulation” Program for Domestic Unlisted Shares of H-share Listed
Companies (《H股公司境內未上市股份申請“全流通”業務指引》) (the “Guidelines for the ‘Full
Circulation’”) latest amended by CSRC on August 10, 2023, the Measures for Implementation of
H-share “Full Circulation” Business (《H股“全流通”業務實施細則》) jointly announced by China
Securities Depository and Clearing Corporation Limited, (“the CSDC”) and Shenzhen Stock
Exchange on December 31, 2019, and the Guidelines on H share “Full Circulation” of CSDC
Shenzhen Branch (《中國證券登記結算有限責任公司深圳分公司H股“全流通”業務指南》) issued
by the CSDC Shenzhen Branch in September 2024, as well as the Guidelines on H share “Full
Circulation” CSDC HK (《中國證券登記結算(香港)有限公司H股“全流通”業務指南》) issued by
the CSDC HK in September 2024.
According to the Guidelines for the “Full Circulation”, shareholders of domestic unlisted
shares may determine by themselves through consultation the amount and proportion of shares, for
which an application will be filed for circulation, provided that the requirements laid down in the
relevant laws and regulations and set out in the policies for state-owned asset administration,
foreign investment and industry regulation are met, and the corresponding H-share listed company
may be entrusted to file with the CSRC for “full circulation”. An unlisted domestic joint stock
company may file with the CSRC for “full circulation” at the time of its initial public offering and
listing overseas. After domestic unlisted shares are listed and circulated on the Stock Exchange,
they may not be transferred back to China. Pursuant to the Overseas Listing Trial Measures, which
came into effect on March 31, 2023, for a domestic company directly offering and listing overseas,
shareholders of its domestic unlisted shares applying to convert such shares into shares listed and
tradedonanoverseastradingvenueshallconformtorelevantregulationspromulgatedbytheCSRC
and authorize the domestic company to file with the CSRC on their behalf.
REGULATIONS RELATING TO CYBERSECURITY, DATA SECURITY AND PERSONAL
INFORMATION PROTECTION
Regulations on Cybersecurity, Data Security and Personal Information Protection
On November 7, 2016, the SCNPC promulgated the Cybersecurity Law of the PRC (《中華
人民共和國網絡安全法》), which became effective on June 1, 2017. The Cybersecurity Law
requires network operators to comply with laws and regulations and fulfill their obligations to
safeguard security of the network when conducting business and providing services. The
Cybersecurity Law further requires network operators to take technical measures and other
necessary measures in accordance with applicable laws, regulations and compulsory national
requirements to safeguard the safe and stable operation of the networks, respond to cybersecurity
incidents effectively, prevent illegal and criminal activities on the network, and maintain the
integrity, confidentiality and availability of network data.
The Data Security Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國數據安全法》), which was
promulgated by the SCNPC on June 10, 2021 and took effect on September 1, 2021, provides that
China shall establish a data classification and grading protection system, formulate the important
data catalogs to enhance the protection of important data. The conduct of data handling activities
shall be in compliance with the provisions of laws and administrative regulations, establishing and
completing a data security management system for the entire workflow, organizing and conducting
data security education and training, adopting corresponding technical measures and other
necessary measures to ensure data security, strengthening risk monitoring, taking immediately
– 89 –

=== PAGE 99 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
disposition measures and promptly reporting to relevant authorities when data security incidents
occur. Processors of important data shall specify the person responsible for data security and
managementagencies,implementdatasecurityprotectionresponsibilities,periodicallyconductrisk
assessments of such data handling activities as provided and submit risk assessment reports to the
relevantauthorities.IfanycompanyviolatestheDataSecurityLawofthePRCandotherapplicable
measures to provide important data outside China, such company may be punished by
administration sanctions, including penalties, fines, and/or suspension of relevant business or
revocation of the business license.
The Personal Information Protection Law of the PRC (《中華人民共和國個人信息保護法》)
(the “PIPL”), which was promulgated by the SCNPC on August 20, 2021 and took effect on
November 1, 2021, integrates the scattered rules with respect to personal information rights and
privacy protection. The PIPL aims at protecting the personal information rights and interests,
regulating the processing of personal information, ensuring the orderly and free flow of personal
information in accordance with the law, and promoting the reasonable use of personal information.
Personal information, as defined in the PIPL, refers to information related to identified or
identifiable natural persons and recorded by electronic or other means, but excluding anonymized
information.The PIPLprovides the conditions under which a personal information processor could
process personal information, which include but are not limited to, where the consent of the
individual concerned is obtained and where it is necessary for the conclusion or performance of a
contract to which the individual is a contractual party. It also stipulates certain specific rules with
respect to the obligations of a personal information processor, such as to inform the purpose and
method of processing to the individuals, and the obligation of the third party who has access to the
personal information by way of co-processing or delegation.
On September 24, 2024, the State Council promulgated the Regulation on Network Data
Security Management (《網絡數據安全管理條例》), which came into effect on January 1, 2025.
TheRegulationonNetworkDataSecurityManagementprovidethatnetworkdataprocessorswhose
network data processing activities affect or may affect national security shall be subject to national
security review in accordance with relevant national regulations.
Regulations on Cybersecurity Review
On December 28, 2021, the Cyberspace Administration of China (the “CAC”), NDRC, the
MIIT and ten other PRC regulatory authorities jointly issued the Cybersecurity Review Measures
(《網絡安全審查辦法》), effective on February 15, 2022. The Cybersecurity Review Measures
require that, (i) any procurement of network products and services by critical information
infrastructure operators, which affects or may affect national security, (ii) any data processing
activities by network platform operators, which affects or may affect national security, (iii) any
network platform operators which has personal information of more than one million users and is
going to be listed abroad, shall be subject to cybersecurity review.
Regulations on Cross-border Data Transfer
OnJuly7,2022,theCACpromulgatedtheMeasuresfortheDataExportSecurityAssessment
(《數據出境安全評估辦法》), which took effect on September 1, 2022. The Measures for the Data
Export Security Assessment requires the data processor providing data overseas and falling under
any of the following circumstances apply for the data export security assessment by the national
cybersecurity administration authority through its local provincial counterpart: (i) where the data
processor intends to provide important data overseas; (ii) where the critical information
infrastructureoperatorandanydataprocessorwhohasprocessedpersonalinformationofmorethan
1,000,000 people intend to provide personal information overseas; (iii) where any data processor
who has provided personal information of 100,000 people or sensitive personal information of
10,000 people to overseas recipients accumulatively since January 1 of the last year intends to
provide personal information overseas; and (iv) other circumstances where the security assessment
of data cross-border transfer is required as prescribed by the CAC.
According to the Measures for the Standard Contract for Outbound Cross-Border Transfer of
Personal Information (《個人信息出境標準合同辦法》) issued by the CAC on February 22, 2023,
and became effective on June 1, 2023, to provide personal information to an overseas recipient
through a Standard Contract executed, a personal information processor shall meet the following
criteria: (i) not being a critical information infrastructure operator; (ii) handling personal
information of fewer than one million individuals; (iii) having provided personal information of
fewer than 100,000 individuals in aggregate to overseas recipients since January 1 of the previous
– 90 –

=== PAGE 100 ===
REGULATORY OVERVIEW
year; and (iv) having provided sensitive personal information of fewer than 10,000 individuals in
aggregate to any overseas recipients since January 1 of the previous year. Where it is otherwise
provided in any law or administrative regulations, or by the national cyberspace authority, those
provisions shall prevail.
On March 22, 2024, the CAC issued the Provisions on Facilitating and Regulating
Cross-border Data Flows (《促進和規範數據跨境流動規定》). In accordance with these
provisions, data processors who provide data abroad, and meet any of the following conditions, are
required to declare the data export security assessment with the national cybersecurity
administration authority through its local provincial counterpart: (i) critical information
infrastructure operators providing personal information or important data abroad; (ii) data
processors other than critical information infrastructure operator providing important data abroad
orcumulativelyprovidingabroadpersonalinformation(withoutanysensitivepersonalinformation)
of more than one million individuals, or sensitive personal information of more than 10,000
individuals since January 1 of the current year.Additionally, to provide personal information to an
overseas recipient through a standard contract executed or with a personal information protection
certification, a personal information processor shall meet the following criteria: (i) cumulatively
exportingpersonalinformation(excludingsensitivepersonalinformation)ofmorethan100,000but
fewer than 1 million individuals since January 1 of the current year; or (ii) cumulatively exporting
sensitive personal information of fewer than 10,000 individuals since January 1 of the current year.
Besides the above, the Provisions on Facilitating and Regulating Cross-border Data Flows also
provide certain circumstances under which the data processors are exempted from carrying out the
data export security assessment or standard contract/personal information protection certification
requirements, loosening the regulations over personal information data cross-border transfer.

diverse background and investment experience. The Pre-IPO

3. Special Rights of the Pre-IPO Investors
The Pre-IPO Investors have been granted certain special rights in relation to our Company,
including, among others, redemption rights, anti-dilution rights, co-sale rights, rights of first
refusal, information rights and recommendation rights.
 Special rights granted by the Company: From 2020 to 2024, the Company issued
Shares with preferred rights (including redemption rights, anti-dilution rights and
preferential liquidation rights) granted by the Company to pre-IPO investors for series
Pre-Ato Series C++ Financings (but not series D, D+, and D++). In accordance with the
Company’s accounting policies, such Shares gave rise to assumed debt obligations and
were initially recognized as financial liabilities at FVTPL.
In November 2024, the Company and all then shareholders, other than Shenwan
Chuangtou, entered into a shareholders’ agreement pursuant to which all redemption
rights, anti-dilution rights and preferential liquidation rights granted to the relevant
Pre-IPO Investors by the Company were terminated and became null and void, and shall
not be reinstated with immediate effect.As a result, except for the 612,274 Shares held
by Shenwan Chuangtou, all Shares with preferred rights were converted into ordinary
shares on a 1:1 basis as of December 31, 2024. In March 2025, before the joint stock
conversion, Shenwan Chuangtou transferred its 612,274 Shares to Jiaxing Chenzhi.
Following such transfer, the remaining Shares with preferred rights were converted into
ordinary shares on a 1:1 basis upon the release of preferred rights, and the related
financial liabilities at FVTPLwere fully derecognized as of June 30, 2025. See Note 31
to the Accountants’ Report as Appendix I to this Prospectus for more details.
 SpecialrightsgrantedbytheControllingShareholders:theControllingShareholders
have granted the redemption rights (except for Jiaxing Chenyi), anti-dilution rights,
priority allocation right for entire sale to all Pre-IPO Investors. Such redemption rights
have been terminated prior to the first submission of listing application to the Stock
Exchange, and all other special rights so granted shall be terminated upon the Listing.
The Company was not a party to such redemption rights and did not provide any
guarantee in respect of the redemption rights granted by the Controlling Shareholders;

PUBLIC FLOAT AND FREE FLOAT
Following the conversion of the Unlisted Shares into H Shares and upon completion of the
Global Offering (assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not exercised):
(a) a total of 78,488,042 H Shares, representing 53.08% of our share capital in aggregate
and held by our core connected persons will not be counted towards the public float,
including our Controlling Shareholders, entities controlled by our Controlling
Shareholders, Xinghang Entities (including Minxi Xinghang, Xinghang Chaozhi,
Xinghang Chaoguang, Xinghang Qiguang, Xinghang Chaofeng and Xinghang Qixin),
entities controlled by Shanghai Chentao (including Huzhou Yuecheng, Jiaxing Kelong,
Jiaxing Chenzhi, Pingtan Jiayi, Jiaxing Chenyi, Chuangxiang Chuangye and Yitao
Chuangye), entities controlled by Zijin Mining (including Zidi Investment, Ziniu
Investment, Zixing Investment and Qihang Investment) and Chentao Xinghang. For
details, see “— Capitalization” below;

(b) a total of 43,249,727 Unlisted Shares held by the remaining existing Shareholders will
be converted into H Shares and listed on the Stock Exchange, and therefore will be
countedaspartofthepublicfloat,representing29.25%ofoursharecapitalinaggregate

as part of the public float, representing 16.47% of our share capital upon the completion
of Global Offering in aggregate.
Based on the above, it is expected that immediately following completion of the Global
Offering (assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not exercised), a total of 69,381,727 Shares,
representing 45.72% of our total share capital upon the completion of the Global Offering
(assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not exercised) will be counted as part of the public
float.
Assuming that the Over-allotment Option is not exercised, (i) if the Offer Price is fixed at
HK$81.16 per H Share (being the low-end of the indicative Offer Price range set out in this
Prospectus), the expected market capitalization of the Company upon Listing would be
approximately HK$12.0 billion, and the percentage that would result in the expected market value
ofHSharesheldbythepublictobeHK$1.5billionatthetimeofListingisapproximately12.50%;
(ii) if the Offer Price is fixed at HK$84.54 per H Share (being the mid point of the indicative Offer
Price range set out in this Prospectus), the expected market capitalization of the Company upon
Listing would be approximately HK$12.5 billion, and the percentage that would result in the
expected market value of H Shares held by the public to be HK$1.5 billion at the time of Listing
is approximately 12.00%; and (iii) if the Offer Price is fixed at HK$87.92 per H Share (being the
upper-end of the indicative Offer Price range set out in this Prospectus), the expected market
capitalization of the Company upon Listing would be approximately HK$13.0 billion, and the
percentage that would result in the expected market value of H Shares held by the public to be
HK$1.5 billion at the time of Listing is approximately 11.54%. Accordingly, the minimum
prescribedpublicfloatpercentageapplicabletoourHSharesunderRule19A.13A(1)oftheListing
Rulesis15%.Therefore,ourCompanywillbeabletosatisfytheminimumpublicfloatrequirement
under Rule 19A.13A of the Listing Rules as over 15% of our Company’s total issued Shares will
be held by the public upon completion of the Global Offering.
On the basis that (i) save as disclosed above, no Offer Shares will be allocated under the
Global Offering to any core connected person of our Company or person which is not regarded as
a member of the public under Rule 8.24 of the Listing Rules and (ii) all Offer Shares to be issued
to the cornerstone investors (if any) are excluded for the purpose of satisfying the free float
requirement (assuming the Over-allotment Option is not exercised), upon the completion of the
Global Offering, it is expected that at least 13,066,000 H Shares, which will be all the Offer Shares
not being subscribed by the cornerstone investors, representing a market capitalization of
HK$1,060.44 million (assuming an Offer Price of HK$81.16 per Offer Share, being the low-end of
the indicative Offer Price range set out in this Prospectus), will not be subject to any disposal
restrictions (whether under contract, the Listing Rules, applicable laws or otherwise) at the time of
the Listing, which will satisfy the free float requirement under Rule 19A.13C(1)(b) of the Listing
Rules.

OVERVIEW
We focus on the commercial deployment of mining autonomous driving solutions in the
mining industry and were among the earlier entrants in autonomous mining transportation. Our
solutions are designed to address the specific operational needs of mining sites, particularly in
environments where mining environment is complex, labor resources are limited, and safety
requirements are high.
According to Frost & Sullivan:
 We ranked first among all commercial vehicle intelligent driving companies by revenue
in China in 2025;

mining trucks as of December 31, 2025;
 We are the first and the only company in the world to have deployed a fleet of over
2,500 active autonomous mining trucks in 2025;
 As of December 31, 2025, we led the industry in terms of cumulative autonomous
haulage volume, autonomous mileage, and completed haulage cycles, and our solutions
have been deployed in the field for over six years with a consistent safety record; and
 In 2025, we held a market share of approximately 37.6% by revenue in China’s mining
autonomous driving solution market, ranking the first in the country; during the same
period, China was the world’s largest market for mining autonomous driving solutions,
accounting for over 50.0% of the global market by revenue.
Wewereearlytorecognizethepotentialforscaledadoptionofautonomousminingandmoved

tailored for mining operations. Our proprietary technologies span areas such as intelligent
perception, prediction, planning and control, and a flexible, software-defined driving architecture,
enabling highly adaptive, scalable, and stable deployment in complex mining environments.
According to Frost & Sullivan, in China’s mining autonomous driving solution market:
 We are among the first companies in mining autonomy to adopt a multi-modal
perception architecture.
 We are the only company enabling full commercial vehicle intelligent driving, real-time
coordination of mixed-traffic, mixed-load, and mixed-dump operations, solving one of
the hardest problems in autonomous logistics: dynamic, multi-agent interaction in open
pit mining sites. Since September 2024, our prediction models ranked #1 in the Multi
World Forecasting leaderboard of the Argoverse2 Motion Forecasting Challenge, a

 We developed mass-produced, drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform for 100-

autonomous mining trucks are capable of increasing transmission efficiency and

 With a standardized, modular architecture, we can complete the deployment of our
solutionsonanewminingsiteinaslittleasthreedays,enablingtheautonomousmining

Market Challenges, Trends, and Our Solution
Mining is a high-stakes, high-cost industry defined by harsh conditions and remote
geographies. Operations are often located at high altitudes or in rugged mining environment, where
workers face extreme weather, shifting ground conditions, and long hours of repetitive labor on
rough mining environment. These realities contribute to chronic labor shortages, high turnover,
safety incidents, and escalating operational costs.
Governments, regulators, and mine operators are aligned on one goal: transitioning to
unmanned operations as a path to improved safety, cost-efficiency, and long-term sustainability.
Butbuildingforminingautonomydemandsafull-stacksolution,fromhardwaretoperception
to control, and deep domain expertise. Most autonomous driving companies lack the technology
robustness, adaptability, and platform-level integration to succeed in this environment. Meanwhile,
most traditional mining equipment manufacturers are not software-native and struggle to deliver
intelligent automation at scale. As a result, very few players globally can deliver autonomy for
mining at scale. As the industry enters a rapid expansion phase, both in China and globally, we
believe our field experience, and stable customer base allows us to capitalize on the growth
opportunities emerging across global mining autonomy adoption.
A Market with Significant Growth Potential
Mining is one of the few commercial applications where autonomous driving has already
reached meaningful scale. According to Frost & Sullivan, mining has outpaced other autonomous
verticals in terms of commercial adoption.
1 “Fully driverless mode” is defined as operating unmanned for over 95% of its daily operating hours, with the
remaining less than 5% of manned time primarily attributable to non-transportation activities such as maintenance,
refueling, or other operational support tasks.

BUSINESS
 China: After early adoption of autonomous driving technologies by leading mining
groups as our customers in 2023, the market is now entering a rapid scale-up phase.The
sales penetration rate of autonomous mining trucks is expected to rise from around 12%
in 2025 to over 50% by 2030, unlocking explosive growth. The market of mining
autonomous driving solutions in China reached RMB3.8 billion in 2025, representing a
CAGR of 171.4% from 2021 to 2025.
 Global: Major mining regions beyond China, including Australia, Canada, and Chile,
face increasing pressure from both rising labor costs and resource constraints. We
believe these markets represent the next wave of growth. Globally, the market size in
terms of revenue for mining autonomous driving solutions is expected to grow from
US$1.0 billion in 2025 to US$7.3 billion in 2030, representing a CAGR of 47.4%. In
Australia alone, the market size in terms of revenue for mining autonomous driving
solutions is projected to exceed US$2.9 billion in 2030.
Beyond offering autonomous driving technologies, we address the structural challenges that
have long constrained efficiency and safety in the mining industry.
Our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions, branded as
ORCASTRA, are the first fully integrated autonomy stack purpose-built for mining haulage in
China. ORCASTRA combines drive-by-wire trucks that equipped with electronic controlling
systems, our proprietary commercial vehicle intelligent driving system and a fleet management and
operations platform, all designed to scale across diverse mining sites and use cases. We have
extended our capabilities with Conductor Plus, our Mining Digitalization Solutions for upgrading
traditional mining equipment with intelligent functions across operations such as excavation,
haulage, and dumping.
Together, ORCASTRA and Conductor Plus enable us to serve a broad spectrum of mining
automation and digitalization needs. Our modular approach supports flexible configurations for
different customer requirements, while our software and operations stack enables cross-sell
opportunities and long-term integration into our customers’ workflows.
Flexible Delivery Models Built for Scale
Weofferadual-productstrategywithflexibledeliverymodelstomeettheoperationalrealities
and procurement preferences of mining customers around the world.
 ORCASTRA: Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and
Solutions.ORCASTRAisdesignedtoautomateminingtransport,acrosscoal,metal,and
quarrysites,underbothstandardandextremeworkingconditions.Iteliminatestheneed
for human drivers, improves safety, and delivers consistent operational efficiency at
scale. ORCASTRA is offered under two commercial models:
– Customer-provided fleet model: Customers possess the mining trucks, equipped
with drive-by-wire electronic controlling chassis fully compatible with our mining
autonomous driving solutions. We provide customers with a full spectrum of
mining autonomous driving services, including the necessary software and
hardware and ongoing maintenance technical support. This model reduces our
upfront capital expenditure and gives customers more flexibility, especially in
vehicle selection, while ensuring our system performance and safety standards are
met through design validation.
– Company-provided fleet model: We possess and manage the autonomous fleet and
provide full-lifecycle support, including deployment, daily maintenance, and
technical update, that continuously drives mining efficiencies. This model is ideal
for customers seeking a fully managed solution with minimal internal resources,
often used in strategic projects and early benchmark deployments.
 Conductor Plus: Mining Digitalization Solutions. Conductor Plus is designed to
upgrade traditional mining equipment and workflows. Conductor Plus enhances key
operational functions, such as production management, safety management, and asset
management, enabling real-time decision-making for both autonomy sites and non-
autonomy sites. We launched Conductor Plus in 2023, and it has since seen strong early
traction.

Our Core Capabilities
Leveraging the expertise and sustained engagement in the autonomous mining, we have built
the following three core capabilities:
 Full-stack system integration, from software to hardware. Our autonomy platform is
built entirely in-house, from commercial vehicle intelligent driving algorithms to
drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform and custom vehicle electronics. Our
architecture is designed to enable precision control, rapid response, and high reliability.
The result is a modular, scalable platform that supports multiple vehicle types and
diverse mining conditions, supporting over 70 vehicle types as of December 31, 2025.
For details, see “— Technology and Research & Development — Flexible Software
Platform — ’Yushi’:AUnified Drive-by-wire Electronic Controlling Platform Purpose-
built for Mining Autonomy”.
 Deep operational insight and field-proven experience. We are the only team in the
industry with large-scale deployment experience across multiple types of high-value
mining, dynamic mixed-fleet operations, and high-altitude environments and the ability
to implement our expertise to non-coal mines. We not only simulate but also design,
deliver, and operate autonomy systems in some of the toughest conditions on earth. We
believe this gives us insight into customer pain points and engineering realities.
 Self-reinforcing AI-model. With several years of R&D and deployment history, we
continuously refine ourAI models and control systems. Our core system has undergone
three major generations and over 100 iterative releases, compounding our technical
capabilities with every deployment.
Commercialization Capabilities
Our business model is built for flexibility and scale. In early stages, we led deployment under
a Company-provided fleet model, possessing the vehicles and offering turnkey operations to help
customers de-risk early adoption. As our technology matured and customer confidence grew, we
shifted toward a higher-margin customer-provided fleet model, allowing customers to procure and
operate their own fleets powered by our technology.
From 2023 to 2025, our total revenue grew from RMB270.9 million to RMB1,435.3 million
in 2025, representing a CAGR of 130.2%. In particular, we launched our customer-provided fleet
model in 2023 that features the light-asset nature and typically requires less costs associated with
owning our autonomous mining truck fleets.
We have established influence and track record among large, strategic customers, particularly
China’s leading mining groups and their contractors. As of December 31, 2025, we had 13 end
customer groups, and our technology has been deployed across 30 mining sites of leading mining
groupsincludingCHNEnergy,SPIC,TBEA,ZijinMining,ShougangGroup,GuanghuiEnergy,and
Baowu Group.

Our Growth Strategy: From Pilot Projects to Scaled Deployment
We are scaling through a repeatable playbook: land a flagship, prove the economics, scale the
fleet, then expand the footprint.
 Deepening penetration in core use cases. In 2023, we launched the world’s largest
single-site autonomous haulage fleet in a coal mine, establishing a flagship benchmark
for the industry. Since then, we have deployed our solutions at nine large-scale mining
sites, each with over 100 autonomous mining trucks. We plan to replicate this success
across additional sites to further increase fleet size and customer retention.
 Expanding into higher-complexity mining environments. Improvements in perception,
planning, and vehicle control have enabled us to extend into metal and quarry mines. In
2024, we launched the first autonomous deployment in Zijin Mining’s Zijinshan
copper-gold mine. In addition, we have further deployed our solutions in Zijin’s
lead-zincmines,Shougang’sironmines,Baowu’sironoperations,andtheJulongcopper
mine at over 5,000 meters above sea level, China’s highest-altitude autonomous mining
deployment to date.
 Targeting high-value overseas markets. Although our business are mainly conducted in
China, we are actively targeting high-value overseas markets. Australia is our first
international priority, selected for its mature mining sector, high labor costs, stable
customer base, and openness to autonomy. We established our Australia office and
signed a memorandum of understanding with MACA (a member of the Thiess group),
one of Australia’s largest general mining contractors in 2023. In 2024, we signed a
memorandum of understanding with Thiess, one of the world’s largest mining service
providers and partnered with Norton Gold Fields (a Zijin subsidiary) to begin localized
product trial project in Kalgoorlie,Australia. This deployment is expected to serve as a
strategic blueprint for overseas expansion.
Our Value Propositions — Exploring the Value of Autonomous Driving in Mining
We offer more than autonomous driving solutions. We also deliver safer workforces, greener
operations, and more resilient industrial systems for the different stakeholders in the mining
industry.
 Safety. Mining is one of the most hazardous industries on earth. Our autonomous
systems remove human operators from dangerous environments, eliminating the risks of
fatigue, distraction, and human error. Safety is engineered into every layer of our stack,
from perception and planning to operational workflows and system redundancy.
 Operation with less carbon footprints. We are committed to the transition to cleaner,
lower-emission mining. We were the first in China to commercially deploy both
range-extended and fully electric autonomous mining trucks at scale in mining sites,
according to Frost & Sullivan. For example, our extended-range EL100 autonomous
mining truck delivers a 25-30% improvement in fuel efficiency compared to traditional
diesel models(1), and each vehicle achieves an annual carbon dioxide reduction of
3,978.5 kilograms(2).
 Productivity addressing labor shortage. Autonomy unlocks more than safety and
sustainability—itunlocksprofits.Oursystemsoperatethroughnight,weather,andshift
changes, smoothing workflows and increasing operational continuity. In mines where
labor is scarce and mining environment is unforgiving, autonomy expands what’s
possible. We enable customers to tap into harder-to-access reserves and extend
productive zones.
 Innovations that have a lasting positive impact on the industry. We have delivered
multiple first-of-its-kind deployments and have been recognized by national authorities
including the MIIT and the National Mine Safety Administration. We collaborate with
top academic institutions and research labs to move the frontier forward, turning
research into operational fleets. We are also a founding partner of the Key Laboratory
for Intelligent and Safe Non-coal Open-pit Mining of the National Mine Safety
Administration (非煤露天礦山安全智能開採國家礦山安全監察局重點實驗室), a
national-level research facility focused on advancing safety and automation in non-coal
open-pit mining in China.

Our Strengths
We have fundamental strengths as follows:
Proprietary Autonomous Driving Technologies and R&D Capabilities
We have developed a vertically integrated autonomy platform that combines precise
perception,advancedvehiclecontrol,andscalablesystemsarchitecture,purpose-builtforminingat
industrialscale.Oursystemisamongthefirstintheindustrytointegratevision-centricmulti-modal
perception, BEV (bird’s-eye view) LiDAR fusion, and occupancy grid-based reasoning. This
combination delivers unmatched perception performance in extreme visibility conditions and
enables generalizable obstacle understanding.
We also lead in interaction. Our model-based trajectory prediction, paired with search-based
decision making and optimization-driven motion planning, gives us advantages in dynamic
multi-agent environments. We are the first in the industry to achieve fully autonomous
“mixed-fleet” operations — simultaneous coordination of different truck and device types across
loading, hauling, and dumping. Since September 2024, our self-developed joint prediction
framework has been ranking the first globally in the Multi World Forecasting leaderboard of the
Argoverse2 Motion Forecasting Challenge, validating our strength in behavior prediction.
The foundation of autonomy is control — and control starts with the chassis. We engineered
the industry’s first drive-by-wire electronic controlling chassis platform for 100-tonne electric
autonomous mining trucks, supported by a self-designed EE architecture and in-house brake and
steering-by-wire systems, giving us precise, responsive, and safe control with reduced system
complexity and cost. Our chassis platform enables rapid software iteration across vehicle types and
supports diverse mining use cases. As of December 31, 2025, 2,580 active autonomous mining
trucksacrossover70customconfigurationshavebeenmass-producedwithourplatform,thelargest
autonomous mining fleet in the world.
Thistechnologyisbuiltbyacross-disciplinaryteamofmorethan300engineersandscientists
across autonomy, software, vehicle systems, simulation, infrastructure, and safety. Our team
includes experts in computer science, electrical and electronics systems, vehicle engineering, new
energy powertrain design, united by the goal of solving some of the most complex technical
challenges in mining autonomy. We collaborate closely with leading universities, national
laboratories, and research institutions to bridge academic research with field deployment. We
believe these partnerships form the foundation of an open and extensible innovation engine,
enabling long-term breakthroughs in autonomy, safety, and intelligent mining.
As of December 31, 2025, we had 242 granted patents in the PRC as well as 43 PCT
applications. Our R&D investments continue to scale with our ambition, with R&D expenses of
RMB177.3 million, RMB208.4 million and RMB270.5 million in 2023, 2024 and 2025,
respectively.

BUSINESS
Full-Stack Solution for Safer, Smarter, and Scalable Mining Autonomy
We offer the comprehensive and production-ready full-stack autonomy solution for mining,
built around two core components: ORCASTRA and Conductor Plus.
ORCASTRA is our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions.
These solutions are powered by our autonomous driving technologies, a modular drive-by-wire
electronic controlling chassis platform, proprietary E/E architecture, and a cloud-connected
dispatch and coordination system. Together, these components enable end-to-end automation, from
perception to execution to mine-level scheduling.
Our drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform supports critical autonomous control
components — braking, steering, and acceleration, and is protocol-compatible with more than 30
different truck models, autonomy across diverse mixed fleets with minimal friction. With the
extensive scenario library and case data from commercial deployments, we support rapid,
site-specific customization for faster time-to-autonomy and greater operational resilience.
Conductor Plus complements ORCASTRA by enhancing core mining workflows, including
excavation, transport, dumping, with AI-based intelligence, coordination, and visualization tools.
Safety is paramount in mining operations. That is why our solutions are purpose-built for
safety at every layer:
 Built-in redundancy. Our platform includes four-layer redundant sensing, six-level
braking protection, and dual-path redundancy across perception, decision-making,
control, and computing.
 Standards-compliant by design.We are among the first in the mining autonomy space to
be certified to ISO 26262 (ASILD) for functional safety and ISO 27001 for information
security. Our development follows the ASPICE framework.
 Advanced safety management systems. With years of field deployment, we have
developed a complete safety management framework by codifying over 30 equipment-
level safety protocols, eight operational SOPs, and 11 specialized safety programs into
standard site execution.
Our technology is designed not only to automate but to outperform traditional workflows.
Autonomous mining trucks equipped with our solutions average over 21 hours of daily operation,
representing approximately 10% improvement over human-driven benchmarks. With Conductor
Plus’sintelligentscheduling,dynamiccoordination,andcontinuousmodeloptimization,wedeliver
108% of human-level transport efficiency in commercial deployment.
ORCASTRA’smodularOSandchassisdevelopmentplatformallowforrapidadaptationacross
trucksizes,energysystems,sensorsuites,anddeploymentenvironments,allowingustoshortenthe
deployment period from delivery to safety-operator-free operation to just three days. Conductor
Plus’s central control platform supports national-standard communication interfaces, enabling
seamless onboarding of diverse trucks, across tonnage classes, energy types, and OEMs, all within
a single unified system.
A Scalable Business Model Fueled by Flagship Deployments and Replications
Our expansion strategy is grounded in a business model built for replication and we focus on
building flagship deployments that scale.
Our technology is field-proven, modular, and deployable across a wide range of mining
environments. This enabled us to achieve rapid market coverage across China, driven by high
transferability across fleets, sites, and use cases. For example,At the largest open-pit coal mine in
China by approved annual capacity, we delivered the industry’s first large-scale 24/7 autonomous
fleet operating across multiple mining blocks. Its success has catalyzed further adoption across the
industry: as of December 31, 2025, nine out of all the 11 mining sites in China operating over 100
autonomous mining trucks were powered by our solutions. Similarly, our solutions have been
successfullydeployedattheworld’shighest-altitudecoppermine,operatedbyaChina-basedglobal
mining conglomerate, where our autonomous fleet has continued to perform reliably despite the
extreme environmental conditions. In another project, at a mine operated by a subsidiary of a
leading listed mining company, we achieved fully autonomous operation without human
intervention for the first time in China. We consider these projects our flagship deployments
primarily as they best demonstrate the robustness, scalability, and commercial maturity of our
autonomous driving solutions across highly challenging operational environments. However, we
typically offer commercial terms and pricing comparable to those applied in other projects.

OUR STRATEGIES
Autonomous mining is evolving, driven by technology trends and rapid adoption. To
capitalize on the opportunities offered by this segment, we are implementing targeted strategies to
enhance our core capabilities and accelerate overseas expansion. These strategies are closely
aligned with our intended use of the net proceeds from the Global Offering, including our planned
investments in software R&D, hardware R&D, information technology development, global
business expansion, customer acquisition, talent development, strategic alliances and selective
acquisitions, and working capital and other general corporate purposes. See “Future Plans and Use
of Proceeds.”
Strengthening Technology Leadership Through Continuous Innovation
We are deepening our full-stack R&D efforts to maintain a innovation in both software and
hardware. To support these initiatives, we intend to apply a significant portion of the net proceeds
from the Global Offering to software R&D, hardware R&D and information technology
development. See “Future Plans and Use of Proceeds — Use of Proceeds — Strengthening
Technology Leadership Through Continuous Innovation — Software R&D,” “— Hardware R&D”
and “— Information technology development.”
 Software and data: We are evolving toward next-generation autonomy architectures,
including end-to-end perception and two-stage planning systems. These upgrades are
designed to improve system performance in unusual or unexpected scenarios. We are
alsoadvancingthefusionofon-boarddatawithV2X(vehicle-to-everything)inputs,and
expanding our site-level AI management platform to support scalable, productized
deployments. To support this evolution, we will continue to accumulate real-world
insight to improve our models to improve our operational capabilities especially in
data-scarce mining environments. These initiatives are expected to be supported by our
planned use of proceeds for software R&D, including the upgrade of our mining
autonomous driving algorithms and the broader applicability of our technologies across
a wider range of environments. See “Future Plans and Use of Proceeds — Use of
Proceeds — Strengthening Technology Leadership Through Continuous Innovation —
Software R&D.”
 Hardware and integration: We are accelerating innovation in drive-by-wire electronic
controlling platforms and critical components, working closely with OEMs to enable
seamless system-level integration. Our roadmap includes next-gen electronic braking
systems, faster electronic steering control, and domain controllers. Over the next three
years, we will focus on extended-range hybrid and all-electric vehicles, while exploring
hydrogen-powered configurations as a future track. We are also developing a purpose-
built cabin-less autonomous mining truck, designed from the ground up for unmanned
mining operations. These initiatives are expected to be supported by our planned use of
proceeds for hardware R&D, including the development of drive-by-wire chassis
platforms, core hardware components, next-generation autonomous mining truck
models, and key vehicle and site-control components. See “Future Plans and Use of
Proceeds — Use of Proceeds — Strengthening Technology Leadership Through
Continuous Innovation — Hardware R&D.”
Expanding Use Cases, Unlocking New Markets
We are scaling across three fronts: deeper penetration in core segments, expanding into new
and complex scenarios, and extending our autonomous driving solutions beyond the mine. Our
planned use of proceeds for software R&D and global business expansion is expected to support
these initiatives, particularly the broader applicability of our technologies across more complex
operating environments, customer acquisition, and overseas expansion. See “Future Plans and Use
of Proceeds — Use of Proceeds — Strengthening Technology Leadership Through Continuous

deployment. Our product roadmap includes increasingly specialized configurations to support cost
efficiency and production flexibility, with the goal of building more site-level benchmarks and
increasing customer reorders and share of wallet over time.

We address this with two core solution suites designed to accelerate mining automation.
 Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions
(ORCASTRA): Our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and
Solutions, collectively branded as ORCASTRA, focus on optimizing the transportation
side of mining operations through the deployment of autonomous mining trucks.
Designed to adapt to a wide range of mining environments, including coal, metal, and
quarry mines, our trucks operate effectively across both simple and highly complex site
conditions. By reducing the need for human drivers, our solutions improve safety, lower
labor costs, and enhance overall operational efficiency.
 Mining Digitalization Solutions (Conductor Plus): Our Mining Digitalization
Solutions leverage data analytics, IoT integration, and real-time monitoring to enhance
every aspect of mining operations. From intelligent fleet management to predictive
maintenance, these solutions streamline operations, maximize productivity, and reduce
costs.
Our two solution suites are both supported by our unified technology infrastructure and
Universal Safety Framework:
 Technology infrastructure: Our technology foundation is purpose-built to support the
scalability, reliability, and long-term evolution of our Closed-EnvironmentAutonomous
MiningTrucks Products and Solutions. It brings together a full stack of core systems —
including our purpose-built autonomous driving algorithms, a modular flexible software
platform,AI development toolchains, intelligent mine operations, and our secure trusted
cloud infrastructure. Each system is engineered for seamless integration and rapid
iteration, enabling faster deployment cycles and stable performance across diverse
mining environments. This architecture gives us the flexibility to adapt quickly to
customer needs while maintaining the robustness required for industrial-grade
operations.
 Universal Safety Framework: At the foundation of our solutions is our proprietary
Universal Safety Framework (USF), a robust system designed to keep operations safe,
stable,andreliable,eveninthemostchallengingminingenvironments.USFspansevery
layer of our solution architecture, from hardware and software to connectivity and
operational protocols, ensuring safety is deeply integrated into every component and
process. This framework is built around a core principle of redundancy, meaning every
critical function is backed by multiple layers of protection.
For more information about our technology infrastructure and the USF, see “— Technology
and Research & Development”.
Our Business Model — how we deliver our solutions and generate revenue
We offer multiple delivery models to meet the diverse needs of our customers, enabling them
to adopt our solutions in ways that best fit their operational goals, financial plans, and management
strategies. Specifically, for our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and
Solutions, customers can choose between two models:
 Customer-provided fleet model: Customers possess the mining trucks, equipped with
drive-by-wire electronic controlling chassis fully compatible with our mining
autonomous driving solutions. We provide customers with a full spectrum of mining
autonomous driving services, including the necessary software and hardware and
ongoing operational and technical support. This model reduces our upfront capital
expenditure and gives customers more flexibility, especially in vehicle selection, while
ensuringoursystemperformanceandsafetystandardsaremetthroughdesignvalidation.
 Company-provided fleet model: We possess and manage the autonomous fleet and
provide full-lifecycle support, including deployment, management, maintenance, and
technical update, that continuously drives mining operational efficiencies.This model is
ideal for customers seeking a fully managed solution with minimal internal resources,
often used in strategic project and early benchmark deployments.

The key distinction between our customer-provided fleet and Company-provided fleet models
lies in whether we — rather than our customers — possess the autonomous mining trucks. Under
our customer-provided fleet model, we do not possess the autonomous mining trucks but only
deploy Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions on the trucks
procured or leased by our customers. Under our Company-provided fleet model, we own or lease
the autonomous mining trucks to provide Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks
Products and Solutions to our customers. Our customers may directly purchase autonomous-ready
trucks from us, or alternatively, only engage us for autonomous driving solutions and related
technology services. In either case, we work with OEMs to source and integrate critical hardware
and software components, such as controllers, drive-by-wire electronic controlling platforms, and
power systems, through processing and assembly arrangements. Under this model, the contractors,
as the mine operators, generally possess the autonomous fleets while we provide the contractors
withautonomousdrivingsolutionsandservices,totransportoresinminingsites.Inthesecases,the
mining companies who own the mining sites are the ultimate end users.

providedfleetmodel.Inadditiontominingcompaniesandcontractorswhoelecttoacquireandown
the autonomous mining trucks, we actively explore business relationships with third-party
companies that engage in leasing business, who acquire autonomous mining trucks for leasing. On

Ourautonomousdrivingsolutionsaredesignedtominimizeon-sitehumaninvolvementwhile
maintaining high levels of operational reliability, scalability, and cost efficiency. By leveraging our
expertiseinautonomousdrivingsystems,standardizedprocessmanagement,andclosecoordination
between technical and operational teams, we are able to manage multiple autonomous mining truck
projects in a safe and efficient manner.
Under our operating model, only a handful and up to approximately 100 personnel are
stationed on site, depending on the complexity, scale and duration of the projects involved. These
primarily include autonomous driving coordinators, operational engineers, post-sales maintenance
personnel, and a small number of managerial staff. Autonomous driving coordinators are
responsible for coordinating our on-site technical and operational teams, streamlining our on-site
service provision. Operational engineers are responsible for overseeing new project deployments,
preparing technical documentation, and monitoring project progress and quality. Post-sales
maintenance personnel handle the upkeep of on-site monitoring systems and other equipment,
respond to customer requests, and ensure stable system performance after deployment.
Our R&D and technical teams generally operate off site, providing centralized, remote
management of autonomous vehicles across projects. On-site full-time employees focus on core
technical and managerial functions such as system scheduling, monitoring, performance
optimization, and project delivery, ensuring the stability, safety, and efficiency of our autonomous
operations. In contrast, outsourced personnel primarily assist with field execution tasks, including
equipment inspection, maintenance, and contingency handling, under the supervision of our
in-house team.

support involves off-site monitoring and troubleshooting of autonomous vehicles and systems.

Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions were still in pilot or early deployment phases.

terminated the foregoing interim arrangement and have since ceased to operate such conventional,
human-operated mining trucks.

Our project cycle begins with identifying potential opportunities, gathering market
intelligence, conducting site visits, preparing solution proposals and defining the scope of work
with prospective customers. If a lead progresses, a formal project is established; if not, we review
the reasons and refine our approach. When projects advance, we conduct qualification reviews,
negotiate and sign contracts, and proceed to delivery and operations, including installing
equipment, testing networks and calibrating systems to support stable performance. After
deployment, we continue to track operational performance, collect customer feedback and
incorporate insights into internal reviews and ongoing product development.

Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions — ORCASTRA
Our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions, collectively
branded as ORCASTRA, are built to transform how materials are transported across mining sites.
The solutions integrate two core components: the autonomous mining trucks, and our proprietary
Autonomous Fleet Management System.
Our Autonomous Fleet Management System serves as the digital command center for
mine-siteautonomy.Itconnectsautonomousminingtrucks,supportequipment,controlcenters,and
cloud platforms, enabling real-time monitoring, dynamic dispatching, and data-driven decision-
making across operations. Seamlessly integrated with our on-vehicleAutonomous Driving System
(ADS), our Autonomous Fleet Management System allows mining operators to reduce manual
intervention and optimize both fleet-level performance and broader site-wide logistics.
A typical deployment of our Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and
Solutions in an open-pit mine is illustrated below:
The cloud and control layer forms the centralized operational backbone of the system.
Through the control room and autonomy management platform, it enables real-time fleet
monitoring, scheduling and production management, supported by 5G connectivity and remote
driver assistance for rare edge cases.
The roadside and infrastructure layer supports on-site autonomous operations. It enables
automated truck parking and dispatch, real-time obstacle avoidance, and optimized loading-zone
coordination through algorithm-driven vehicle alignment and queue management.
Additional infrastructure capabilities enhance system adaptability and coordination. These
include real-time updates as site conditions change and retrofit instrumentation that allows
conventional equipment to operate alongside autonomous fleets.

The following graphics show how our autonomous mining trucks are engineered for

Our autonomous mining trucks are powered by three tightly integrated core systems:
 Autonomous Driving System (ADS): The “brain” of the vehicle, ADS is an AI-driven,
on-vehicle software stack that enables real-time environmental perception, path
planning, and dynamic decision-making. It orchestrates all aspects of autonomous
driving, from obstacle avoidance to route optimization.
 Drive-by-Wire Electronic Controlling Chassis Platform:Acting as the truck’s “muscle,”
this system executes steering, braking, and power commands with high precision and
responsiveness, which is crucial for maintaining safety and control in rugged, high-
intensity mining environments.
 Electrical and Electronic Architecture (EEA): Serving as the truck’s “nervous system,”
the EEA integrates sensors, controllers, signal networks, and data pathways into a
unified architecture that supports seamless communication between hardware and
software components.

Together, these systems form the backbone of a robust, field-proven autonomous driving

Autonomous Driving System (ADS)
Our ADS is engineered for the realities of mining. Supporting mixed operations with
human-operated trucks, the system leverages proprietary prediction and intent-recognition models
to coordinate multi-vehicle interactions, operate in tight spaces, and park with high precision. With
intelligentloading,adaptivedispatch,andcollaborativedumping,theADSscalesacrossminetypes
and geologies, enabling faster deployments and broader adoption across the mining sector.
Our ADS is powered by three foundational technology pillars:
 AdvancedAlgorithms. At the heart of our autonomy stack are proprietary algorithms for
perception, prediction, decision-making, planning and control. These enable vehicles to
“see,” “anticipate,” and “act” in real time, even under the most demanding mine
conditions. For more detail, see “— Technology and Research & Development —
Algorithms — Purpose-Built for Mining Environments”.
 SensorsandDomainControlUnit.Oursensorsuiteincludesradar,LiDAR,cameras,and
other navigation technologies, all fused through an onboard domain controller purpose-
built for autonomy. This controller is the vehicle’s decision engine: it continuously
interprets sensor data, understands surroundings, plans motion, and sends control
commands.
 Built-In Safety with Multi-Layer Redundancy. Our system is designed with safety as a
first principle, equipping each truck with multiple layers of redundant sensors and
computing. Full 360° coverage is achieved via cameras, LiDAR, and millimeter-wave
radar, with independent perception algorithms running in parallel. In low-visibility
conditions, obstacle detection exceeds 95% accuracy within 80 meters. A built-in
diagnostic system simulates over 4,000 failure scenarios to proactively detect and
manage issues, with all safety logic executed at the vehicle level, requiring no cloud
connectivity for fault detection or safe shutdown.
Drive-by-Wire Electronic Controlling Chassis
Drive-by-wire Electronic Controlling Chassis System
Our Drive-by-Wire Electronic Controlling System, the core execution layer of our
autonomous mining trucks, replaces mechanical and hydraulic controls with fully electronic
actuation,enablingprecise,real-timecontroloversteering,braking,andacceleration.Purpose-built
for mining, it is resilient under harsh conditions, integrates seamlessly with our vehicles, and
delivers high accuracy, rapid response, energy efficiency, and system-level fault tolerance. The
system ensures smooth, reliable operation across steep grades, uneven surfaces, and tight loading
areas, unlocking the full potential of autonomous mining.

DCS is powered by the following key elements:
 Proprietary Braking System. Our Intelligent Braking Control System is built with
dual-redundant architecture and integrates both service and parking brake functions.
Designed specifically for mining autonomy, it supports advanced braking and stability
control functions to maintain vehicle stability under low-traction, curved, or heavy
downhill conditions.
 Proprietary Steering System. We use a hybrid electric-hydraulic setup optimized for
responsivenessanddirectionalaccuracyatspeed.Thesystemhitsasub-400msresponse
time, well ahead of the 600-800ms industry norm, according to Frost & Sullivan,
enabling confident, real-time path corrections in large vehicle platforms.
 Proprietary Software Platform. Built with a modular architecture, our software platform
enables cross-vehicle adaptability and rapid deployment. It supports plug-and-play
functionality across different truck models, making it easier to scale and customize for
diverse mining environments.
 Proprietary Diagnostic Platform. The system includes a full-stack diagnostics engine
that monitors vehicle health across cloud, on-board, and component layers. With over
4,000 failure modes mapped and monitored in real time, it provides early warnings,
supports autonomous fault recovery, and improves long-term reliability through
continuous feedback.
 Wire-control Safety Architecture. All motion control, including steering, braking, and
acceleration, is handled electronically. Redundant circuits, real-time health checks, and
intelligent failover protocols ensure that critical functions remain operational in the
event of a fault. This layered approach to safety underpins our commitment to
automotive-grade control integrity.
Electric Drive System (EDS)
In the world of 100-tonnage mining trucks, performance is not just about power, it is about
efficiency, control, and durability under the most sophisticated conditions. We have engineered a
next-gen electric drive system (EDS) from the ground up to meet those exact demands. Unlike
traditional diesel-powered platforms, our system is built for autonomy, modularity, and lifecycle
efficiency.
Key innovations of the EDS include:
 High-Power Auxiliary Power Unit (APU): Our 400kW APU eliminates unnecessary
mechanical components like traditional generators and cooling fans to reduce energy
loss and maintenance. The control system enables dynamic on-off cycling and real-time
power optimization, ensuring the engine operates within its most efficient range under
varying loads.
 Integrated Thermal Management System: Our system combines cooling for the battery,
motors, and controller into a single streamlined setup, cutting component count by
roughly 30% than traditional thermal systems and boosting overall reliability. Built to
performinextremeconditionsfrom-40°Cto55°C,ithandlesdemandingtaskslikelong
uphill hauls and reuses waste heat to improve energy efficiency.
 OptimizedPowertrainArchitecture:Weuseadual-motorlayoutpairedwithasimplified
3-speed transmission, replacing older, more complex gear systems. This makes shifting
smoother, reduces mechanical wear, and improves fuel efficiency, all of which lowers
operating costs over the vehicle’s lifetime.
 Intelligent Energy Management: Our in-house energy strategy uses real-time vehicle
data to fine-tune power usage, optimizing torque, braking, heat control, and generator
output. In the field, this system has delivered over 20% fuel savings as compared to
traditional energy management system, helping reduce costs and keep vehicles running
longer between service intervals.
Electrical and Electronic Architecture (EEA)
Our next-generation electronic and electrical architecture (EEA) is purpose-built for
autonomous mining, unifying driving intelligence, vehicle control, and connectivity into a single
platform. By consolidating systems, it reduces control units by ~30% versus traditional
architectures while enhancing reliability. Its modular software foundation enables faster
deployment, flexible updates, and responsive feature development across vehicle models,
supporting the demands of high-tonnage autonomous operations.
– 144 –

=== PAGE 154 ===
BUSINESS
Our EEA is built around a three-domain architecture, chassis, connectivity, and intelligent
driving, each powered by custom-designed controllers engineered to handle the demands of
autonomous, high-tonnage mining operations. Key components include:
 Autonomous Driving Controller (ADC). The ADC is the central compute platform for
perception, planning, and decision-making. Equipped with a 200-TOPS processor, it
supports sensor fusion across LiDAR, radar, and camera systems, and handles complex
functions such as high-speed NOA (Navigation on Autopilot). Rated to ASIL D and
protected against vibration, water ingress, and condensation, theADC is built to operate
reliably in tough mining conditions.
 Chassis Domain Controller (CDC). Purpose-built for our Drive-by-Wire Electronic
Controlling Chassis Platform, our CDC precisely manages braking, steering, and
accelerating, bridging the gap between decision-making and execution. The unit is built
with dual-redundant chips and meets rigorous safety and environmental standards,
enabling stable operation even in open-pit environments with extreme dust, moisture,
and temperature variation.
 Rear Domain Controller (RDC). Our RDC consolidates multiple vehicle functions,
braking control, tire pressure monitoring, load sensing, and remote operation, into a
single, high-integrity module. By reducing ECU count and wiring complexity, RDC
simplifies system architecture while improving reliability and cost structure.
 Network Domain Controller (NDC). As the vehicle’s communications hub, our NDC
supports 5G and V2X (vehicle-to-everything) protocols to enable real-time interaction
between vehicles, command centers, and on-site personnel.
Development, Manufacturing and Assembly of Autonomous Mining Trucks
Apart from a select number of critical control units that we assemble in-house to ensure
seamless compatibility with our proprietary algorithms and hardware systems, we primarily
collaborate with established OEM partners to assemble the autonomous mining trucks we manage
or deliver to customers. The in-house assembled units primarily include the chassis domain
controller, rear domain controller, and intelligent networked terminal, which are used for vehicle
control and wireless communication. During the Track Record Period, our annual production
capacity for these units was approximately 8,000, 6,000 and 4,000 units, respectively.
In most cases, we specify the design and technical standards, while OEMs provide the
non-powered chassis and perform final assembly. We take the lead in designing and integrating all
key intelligent systems, including the electric powertrain (battery, motor, control units, and thermal
management), chassis systems (braking and steering), and core domain controllers. These
components are sourced from vetted third-party suppliers under our technical standards, and OEMs
are paid a processing fee for assembly and integration.
Toservecustomerswithspecializedoperationalneeds,wealsoco-developcustomizedvehicle
models with OEMs. Such models are factory-integrated and delivered preconfigured for
autonomous deployment. For customers preferring standardized platforms, we adapt our drive-by-
wire chassis systems to pre-existing vehicle models and work with OEMs to integrate them during
production. To ensure consistent quality, all autonomous mining trucks undergo rigorous pre-
delivery inspections against our internal acceptance standards before being cleared for customer
delivery.
Our cooperation models with OEMs can be grouped into five categories, depending on the
division of responsibilities:
 CategoryA:Weinitiateandleadoverallvehicleplanning,includingtheselectionofthe
autonomousdrivingsystem,theelectricsystem,andthedrive-by-wiresystem.TheOEM
provides the chassis and undertakes vehicle manufacturing.
 Category B: The OEM leads overall vehicle planning and design, while we contribute
by developing autonomous driving and drive-by-wire hardware and software.
 Category C: The OEM leads vehicle planning, design, and chassis control programming.
We provide autonomous driving adaptation, with drive-by-wire hardware development
shared between us and the OEM.
 Category D: The OEM is fully responsible for vehicle planning, design, and drive-by-
wire development. Our role is limited to installing our autonomous driving kit and
performing the adaptation work.
 Category E: We retrofit vehicles already delivered to mines by equipping them with
autonomous driving functionality.

We believe that working with OEMs under these flexible cooperation models — rather than
manufacturing complete vehicles in-house — enables us to focus on innovation, product
development, and system integration, while benefiting from OEMs’ scale, efficiency, and
manufacturing expertise. At the same time, we continue to invest in the in-house development of
critical components, particularly chassis platforms and domain controllers, to strengthen our
technical edge, accelerate product iteration, and retain greater control over core technologies.
For the development and manufacturing of key components used in our solutions, we follow
a disciplined process that progresses from planning to design and ultimately to production. During
planning, we establish technology roadmaps for autonomous driving kits and drive-by-wire mining
trucks by benchmarking industry peers, assessing customer needs, and aligning with our long-term
strategy. We then move into design and development, where we define product requirements,
complete detailed hardware and software design, secure intellectual property, and conduct
prototyping and testing until the design is finalized. The final stage is mass production, which
covers manufacturing process design, production line construction, material procurement,
workforce training, trial runs, and quality certification.
Autonomous Fleet Management System (“AFMS”)
OurAFMS supports large-scale unmanned fleet deployment in complex mining environments
through three integrated components. The Intelligent Dispatch System centrally manages
excavation, haulage, and dumping workflows, dynamically scheduling thousands of vehicles,
optimizing routes, and integrating energy logistics for autonomous and manned vehicles. The
Collaborative Field System coordinates autonomous trucks with on-site equipment via V2X
communicationandedgeprocessing,optimizingtasksequencing,reducingidletime,andenhancing
operational safety. The Remote Takeover System allows real-time human intervention under
high-risk conditions, with ultra-low-latency connectivity, cross-model compatibility, and multi-
vehicle supervision, enabling a single operator to manage up to 60 vehicles simultaneously.
