Mining Digitalization Solutions (Conductor Plus)
Building on our experience with autonomous fleets, we developed Conductor Plus, an
AI-powered mining digitalization solution that can be sold and deployed independently, regardless
of whether a customer adopts our Company-provided fleet or customer-provided fleet model
solutions.Designedaroundminingproductionworkflows,ConductorPlussupportskeyoperational
processes, including extraction, transportation, dumping and coordination of manned equipment.
The platform supports staged deployment: early-stage deployments coordinate manned
vehicles, while integration with our ORCASTRA autonomous driving solutions enables unified
control across mixed fleets. As of December 31, 2025, Conductor Plus is at an early
commercialization stage, with contracts secured for full Mining Digitalization Solution
deployments, combining hardware and operational efficiency services.
IMCS (Integrated Mining Management and Control System)
IMCS builds on ourAFMS to provide a unified platform managing the full mining workflow.
It integrates multiple systems and equipment, both autonomous and manned, allowing centralized
control of haulage, loading, and auxiliary tasks. Serving as the digital backbone of our Mining
Digitalization Solutions, IMCS enables full-site automation and coordinated operations. Its
intelligent maintenance system tracks the lifecycle of autonomous trucks and key components,
enabling early detection of issues and preventive maintenance to reduce downtime. Operational
visibility is enhanced through an interactive dashboard that provides real-time insights into
production and equipment performance, along with historical analytics for better decision-making.
Intelligent Truck Dispatch Terminals
Our Intelligent Truck Dispatch Terminals are highly integrated sensing and control units
installed on manned equipment such as loaders, bulldozers, and command vehicles. Our Intelligent
Truck Dispatch Terminals support seamless coordination between manned and unmanned
equipment, including autonomous mining trucks via V2V communication, dispatch of manned
trucks and are connected to the IMCS.
Compared to traditional systems, our Intelligent Truck Dispatch Terminals offer multi-level
access control, which significantly improves automation coverage, safety, and system-level
integration.
CASE STUDIES
Northwest China – Large-Scale Open-Pit Coal Mine Deployment
Located in Northwest China, this open-pit coal mine is among the largest in the country by
approved annual capacity. Here, we run the largest single-site autonomous fleet in the world,
deployed with over 230 active autonomous mining trucks as of December 31, 2024.
Our system enables full-process coal extraction that allows for truly mixed-fleet autonomous
operations in a highly dynamic environment. The site has achieved 24/7 continuous unmanned
haulage and has become a benchmark for intelligent open-pit mine operations in China. The
deployment has not only reduced on-site headcount by more than 200 people per shift, removing
workers from hazardous conditions, but also improved overall productivity by over 95% compared
with manual operations.At the same time, it has cut carbon emissions by an estimated 150 tons per
vehicle per year. Following the success of this project, the customer has expanded our solutions to
other mines within its portfolio.
CNBM — Fushan Quarry
Launched in 2023, the Fushan Quarry, operated by China National Building Material Group
(CNBM), features 20 fully electric autonomous wide-body mining trucks and has achieved stable,
24/7 operations for over two years. It is the first full-site deployment of new-energy autonomous
transportation in China’s quarry sector and ranks among the largest nationwide in operational
scale.

BUSINESS
Our deployment at the Fushan Quarry integrates electric drive systems, autonomy, and
high-speed connectivity to form a modern mining operation built around safety, intelligence, and
low emissions. By reducing labor dependence, the quarry has saved roughly 80% of labor costs,
equal to roughly RMB4.4 million annually. At the same time, the use of fully electric trucks has cut
coal-equivalent consumption by an estimated 140 tons per vehicle per year, significantly lowering
carbon emissions. The site successfully addresses real-world challenges such as mixed-fleet
coordination, adaptive production scheduling, and narrow-area operations, demonstrating the
robustness and flexibility of our solutions in complex, space-constrained environments.
Zijin Mining — Julong Copper Mine
The Julong Copper Mine, located at elevations between 4,000 and 5,400 meters, is China’s
largest porphyry copper deposit, with over 25.88 million tonnes of registered copper resources as
of 2024. It also ranks among the world’s top three copper mines by altitude and haulage belt length
and includes valuable associated deposits of silver and molybdenum.
As part of its transformation into a green, intelligent mining operation, Zijin Mining has
begun scaling autonomous haulage at Julong. We have deployed more than 30 autonomous trucks
at Julong, supported by cloud-based control, positioning stations, roadside infrastructure, and
remote takeover systems. This project, representing the largest autonomous haulage deployment
among China’s open-pit metal mines, has established a new benchmark for large-scale deployment
with significant impact. Autonomous operations have reduced the need for manually operated
trucks, cutting annual labor costs by approximately RMB5.5 million. By removing drivers from
high-altitude environments, the system has enhanced safety while improving overall efficiency.
OUR EXTENSIVE, STRATEGIC USE CASE COVERAGE
As of December 31, 2025, our solutions had been deployed at 30 mining sites across four
major regions in China, including Northwest (14 sites), North China (11 sites), East China (two
sites) and Southwest China (three sites), covering coal mines (23 sites), metal mines (three sites)
and quarries (four sites).
As of December 31, 2025, we had deployed 2,580 active autonomous mining trucks across all
sites. Our solutions were deployed at 19 of the 41 largest open-pit coal mines in China, including
seven of the 12 largest in terms of annual capacity. At two of the largest open-pit coal mines in
China by approved annual capacity, we run the world’s largest single-site autonomous fleet in the
world, each deployed with over 500 active autonomous mining trucks as of December 31, 2025,
achieving enhanced performance in unmanned mileage, material transported, and dispatches,
according to Frost & Sullivan.
Our technology has matured to reliably operate in extreme weather and visibility conditions,
coordinating mixed fleets of autonomous and human-operated equipment. This capability has
enabled expansion beyond coal into quarries and metal mines. For example, at the Fushan Quarry
in Shandong, 23 fully electric autonomous trucks have been operated end-to-end with only two
on-site personnel per shift, with the initial fleet of 20 trucks having accumulated over 23 months
of continuous deployment, demonstrating efficiency and reliability in non-coal deployments.
Since 2024, we have collaborated with Zijin Mining, deploying our solutions across copper,
gold, zinc, and iron mines, including the high-altitude Julong Copper Mine at over 5,000 meters.
Deployments with other major operators such as Shougang and Baowu further validate the
robustness and adaptability of our platform across diverse and challenging mining environments.

OUR CONTINUOUS OVERSEAS ENDEAVOUR
We are expanding internationally with a focused strategy to bring our autonomous mining
technology to high-potential overseas markets. Our goal is to improve operational efficiency and
safety for mining operators worldwide through scalable, proven mining autonomous driving
solutions.
We selected Australia as our first international market due to its unique combination of
operational maturity, economic rationale, and strategic visibility. Australia’s mining industry is
highlyadvanced,withrigoroussafetystandards,reliableoperators,andatrackrecordofembracing
automation. Australia also plays a central role in the global mining industry and is widely
recognized for setting high standards in mining operations and innovation. Success inAustralia not
only offers revenue but also helps to establish global credibility.According to Frost & Sullivan, the
mining autonomous driving solution market inAustralia, with a market size of over US$2.9 billion
in 2030, represents a substantial near-term opportunity, with significant growth potential across a
globalmarketsizeofminingautonomousdrivingsolutionsindustryofoverUS$7.3billionin2030.
We began building our international team in 2022 and opened our Australia office in 2023,
becoming the first and only Chinese autonomous mining technology provider with a formal local
presence,accordingtoFrost&Sullivan.Weestablishedawholly-ownedsubsidiaryinAustraliaand
formed a localized team that covers project delivery, localized product definition, business
development and brand building, consisting of experts with more than ten years of experience in
autonomous haulage. We signed a memorandum of understanding with MACA (a member of the
Thiessgroup),oneofAustralia’slargestend-to-endgeneralminingcontractorsin2023.In2024,we
signed a memorandum of understanding with Thiess, one of the world’s largest mining service
providers, and partnered with Norton Gold Fields (a Zijin Group’s subsidiary) to begin a localized
product trial project in Kalgoorlie,Australia. In this project, we supply retrofit mining autonomous
driving solutions to the first batch of rigid mining trucks of a mainstreamAustralian brand, which
has started trial production in a live production environment recently.Through this project, we aim
to standardize our delivery process and after-sale support model for theAustralian market. We see
this deployment not just as a commercial milestone, but as a strategic beachhead for broader
expansion into other high-value overseas markets. As of the Latest Practicable Date, we have not
generated any revenue relating to Closed-Environment Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and
Solutions in Australia.
To support sustainable international growth, we have built a structured cross-border
operational framework, including compliance systems tailored to local legal and regulatory
requirements, particularly in mining safety, contract performance, and data governance, supported
by local legal advisors. We also maintain on-the-ground service and operations teams to ensure
timely support and after-sales responsiveness.
Our international expansion strategies further include offering more advanced solutions to
accommodateincreasinglycomplexworkingconditions,providingmorecompetitivepricingtohelp
our customers in cost reduction and efficiency improvement, enabling faster and more streamlined
deployment to lower the usage threshold for customers, jointly promoting new energy autonomous
driving solutions with domestic OEMs, and collaborating with ecosystem partners such as Thiess
todelivermorereliablelocalsupport.Webelievewehavethefollowingstrengthinthecompetition
with local existing suppliers: (i) our mining autonomous driving solutions adopt a distributed
architecture and the communication between trucks and cloud is minimal, resulting in low network
dependency and further lowering the infrastructure investment cost for mining automation; (ii) our
distributed architecture enables real-time transit decisions of trucks, allowing for more flexible
routing and more efficient dispatching and improving overall traffic efficiency and capacity; (iii)
our trucks are equipped with autonomous algorithms that allow for rapid deployment in new mines
and increased intelligence over time; (iv) our system has been validated across mines of various
scales, terrains, climate and temperature, able to fully leverage existing mining environments to
achieve autonomous haulage with wide applicability across various mining operations; and (v) our
solutions offer a significant advantage leveraging China’s robust new energy industry chain in the
green transformation in the global mining industry.
Over the next three to five years, we intend to pursue overseas expansion opportunities by
aligning with national initiatives and partnering with leading Chinese mining enterprises in their
international mining deployments, including in Indonesia, Chile, Peru and other major mining
markets.Ourlong-termobjectiveistoestablishourselvesasamainproviderofminingautonomous
driving solutions in the future, with overseas markets expected to become a meaningful contributor
to our overall business.

Flexible Software Platform
We have developed a proprietary, modular software platform that streamlines deployment of
our autonomous mining system across sites and vehicle models. By unifying control logic,
workflows,anddispatchbehaviorintoconfigurablemodules,theplatformadaptstovaryingmining
environments,vehiclespecifications,andenvironmentalconditionswithoutcustomrebuilding.This
approach has significantly reduced integration time, with some deployments achieving fully
autonomous, operator-free operation within three days of vehicle arrival.

Our Flexible Software Platform includes two main capabilities: (i) “Yushi,” our proprietary
unified drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform; and (ii) Intelligent Driving OS.
“Yushi”: A Unified Drive-by-wire Electronic Controlling Platform Purpose-built for Mining
Autonomy
The mining truck market is fragmented by design, different OEMs build on different
electrical/electronic architectures, use proprietary control protocols, and rarely conform to
integration standards. That makes autonomy hard to scale. As trucks grow larger and more
intelligent, this complexity only increases. Historically, autonomous systems had to be custom-fit
to each vehicle model, creating increased integration costs and long deployment cycles.
We built Yushi to break that cycle. Launched in 2023, Yushi is the industry’s first and only
scalable drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform purpose-built for autonomous mining fleets.
Yushi decouples hardware and software by providing a unified, open-standard architecture that sits
on top of OEM-supplied chassis, whether powered or non-powered. The system abstracts away
hardware-specific protocols, enabling autonomous driving software developers to focus purely on
autonomy,notmechanicalintegration.Builtonamodularframework,Yushisupportsfastfunctional
iteration and allows seamless switching between autonomous and manual modes to meet the
evolving needs of mine operators.
As of December 31, 2025, Yushi has been deployed across over 70 vehicle models. The
platform has been adopted by approximately 13 OEM partners, including industry leaders such as
Tonly,LGMG,Yutong,andNHL,demonstratingitshighcompatibility,adaptability,andscalability.
At the largest open-pit coal mine in China by approved annual capacity, for example, our
100-tonnage autonomous electric truck model, powered by the Yushi platform, has achieved
fleet-level deployment with a fault rate below 5%, significantly lower than that of conventional,
mannedautonomousminingtrucks.Theplatformhasdeliveredfuelsavingsofmorethan20%,with
minimal compromise in safety or productivity. Several vehicles have surpassed 100,000 kilometers
of fully autonomous operation, further validating the durability and reliability of Yushi in
high-demand, continuous-use environments.

BUSINESS
Intelligent Driving OS: A Scalable and Flexible Software Development Platform
Ourthird-generationIntelligentDrivingOSisamodularsoftwareplatformdesignedforrapid
deployment of autonomous systems across diverse vehicles, hardware, and mining environments. It
features in-house middleware for modular architecture, hardware-agnostic integration with LiDAR,
radar, cameras, and 4G/5G/C-V2X, centralized configuration management, algorithm adaptability
for task-specific optimization, and support for FOTA and SOTA over-the-air updates, enabling
scalable, flexible, and efficient cross-deployment operations.
Algorithms — Purpose-Built for Mining Environments
Miningenvironmentsaremorechallengingthanhighwaysorcitystreets,characterizedbylow
visibility, rough and unstructured mining environments, and constant interaction with manned
equipment.Sensorsmustoperatethroughdust,fogandrain,whilevehiclesnavigatearounddozers,
water trucks and other obstacles, placing higher demands on perception, planning and real-time
control. Our autonomy stack is designed to address these challenges through integrated perception,
localization, prediction, planning and control systems built for high-interaction mining
environments, supporting safe and efficient fleet-scale deployment. Our purpose-built algorithms
include (i) a vehicle-cloud collaborative architecture, (ii) a multimodal perception system; and (iii)
predictive planning with multimodal trajectory forecasting.
Vehicle-Cloud Collaborative Architecture
Traditional autonomous mining systems have historically relied heavily on centralized,
cloud-based dispatching. We have taken a fundamentally different approach, by designing a
next-generation vehicle-cloud collaborative architecture that prioritizes edge autonomy while
integrating cloud-based intelligence for strategic coordination.
At the core of this design is a layered decision-making framework: real-time perception,
localization, prediction, and control are all executed on the vehicle itself, enabling continuous
operation even in low-connectivity environments. The cloud layer focuses on high-level task
scheduling, fleet coordination, and long-horizon planning. Compared to cloud-dependent legacy
architectures, our system delivers higher operational resilience, better fault tolerance, and
significantly improved adaptability, particularly in remote mining areas where network
infrastructure is limited or intermittent. This architecture is purpose-built to support autonomy at
scale.
Multimodal Perception System
Our proprietary multimodal perception system fuses LiDAR, cameras, and other sensors to
generate a unified, real-time view of the mining environment. Using a deep-learning framework, it
robustly detects obstacles, personnel, and equipment. Optimized for mining, our algorithms
differentiate uneven ground from safe paths and distinguish similarly shaped machinery, improving
path planning and safety. The system maintains high detection accuracy in heavy dust, rain, snow,
poor lighting, or vibration, enabling reliable operation under extreme conditions.
Predictive Planning with Multimodal Trajectory Forecasting
Our deep-learning-based prediction engine anticipates the motion and intent of over 20
dynamic agents, including manned vehicles and mobile equipment, across high-interaction
scenarios like intersections, merging zones, and unstructured roads. It combines trajectory
forecasting with conflict resolution, blind-spot avoidance, and energy-aware path planning to
support safe, stable decision-making in fast-changing mine environments. This capability enables
trucks to operate beyond closed-loop settings, powering mixed-fleet collaboration across the full
load-haul-dump cycle. Our algorithm has been ranking first in the Multi World Forecasting
leaderboardoftheArgoverse2MotionForecastingChallengesinceSeptember2024,makingusthe
only provider in the industry with a proven system for coordinated mixed operations: mixed traffic,
mixed loading, and mixed dumping.
Vehicle Stability Technologies
To ensure traction and balance on slippery, uneven, and sloped surfaces, we developed a
real-time vehicle stability system that integrates anti-slip control with adaptive drive force
distribution. It monitors grip, gradient, and load conditions to adjust speed and body posture on the
fly, keeping trucks stable even in ice, snow, or loose mining environments. This system reduces
skidding and rollback risk while maintaining throughput in challenging environments.
– 152 –

=== PAGE 162 ===
BUSINESS
High-Reliability Localization Technologies with Less Reliance on Prior Information
Traditional autonomous systems rely on prior information and RTK signals, which are often
unreliable in high-altitude or low-connectivity zones. Our system uses a hybrid localization
approach, fusing LiDAR, vision, and inertial information with learned trajectories and improves
adaptability to the diverse mining environments.
AI Development Toolchains
AI Agent-Based Simulation
We have built a simulation framework where virtual vehicles act like real ones, making
independent decisions, reacting to obstacles, and coordinating in dense traffic. Unlike rule-based
simulations, our agent-driven system creates realistic, high-risk scenarios that help uncover edge
cases and stress-test autonomy before real-world deployment.
Test Case Generation Using AIGC Technologies
To accelerate training, we use automated data processing techniques to expand our training
datasets and test cases with diverse operating conditions. This approach enables us to efficiently
produce large volumes of high-quality training data and test cases, improve model robustness
without requiring extensive real-world data.
Self-Reinforced AI Models
Our self-reinforced AI models leverages over six million autonomous trips across complex
mining environments, supporting three software generations and 100+ iterative updates. It captures
high-volume driving data from LiDAR, radar, cameras, vehicle controls, and dispatch systems to
continuously improve perception, prediction, and decision-making. Pre-labeled objects accelerate
annotation, with human review ensuring accuracy, while edge cases are flagged to build a scenario
library for retraining. Real-world cases are simulated to test algorithms under extreme conditions.
Continuous Integration & Deployment Pipeline
Ourtoolchainautomatesthefullsoftwarelifecycle,fromcodetodeployment.Itsupportsboth
scheduled and on-demand builds (CI), runs automated simulation and hardware-in-the-loop tests
(CT), and pushes validated versions directly to deployment environments for staging or release
(CD). This closed-loop system improves speed, consistency, and quality across all deployments.
Intelligent Mine Operations
Weusereal-timeanalyticsandsimulationtechnologytooptimizefleetcoordination,dispatch,
maintenance, and energy planning. Our system integrates live environment and operational data to
support intelligent decision-making. A central dashboard visualizes site activity, enables route
planning, flags anomalies, and allows historical playback for safety review, enabling multi-vehicle
trackingandremotevideoaccess.PredictivemaintenanceleveragesAItomonitorkeycomponents,
forecast failures, and trigger automated tasks, such as optimized tire replacement, reducing
downtime and improving reliability.
Trusted Cloud Infrastructure
We have implemented a secure cloud infrastructure to support large-scale autonomous mining
operations. In 2024, we adopted China’s commercial cryptographic standards and enhanced key
management to ensure safe data transmission under complex network conditions. Our modular
business platform connects workflows across extraction, transport, safety, and maintenance,
enablingrapiddeploymentandreal-timecross-moduleresponses,suchasauto-dispatchadjustments
triggered by safety alerts, to improve operational efficiency and resilience.
Universal Safety Framework (USF)
Safety and reliability are paramount for autonomous mining. The Company’s full-stack
Universal Safety Framework (USF) integrates hardware, software, connectivity, and operational
protocols, embedding redundancy at every layer. Critical functions are backed by overlapping
sensors and independent algorithms, while redundant drive-by-wire architecture and ISO 26262-
compliant safety software ensure functional safety. Operational procedures, site boundaries, and
emergency protocols support scalable, reliable deployment. The USF underpins our solutions,
including our Flexible Software Platform,AI algorithms, Intelligent Mine Operations, and Trusted
Cloud Infrastructure, ensuring safe and resilient operations across all mining sites.

R&D Team and Capabilities
We have established a proprietary R&D platform supported by leading universities and
research institutions, focused on autonomous driving and vehicle development, including
operational efficiency, drive-by-wire systems, core hardware reliability and software-hardware
integration through systems. As of December 31, 2025, our R&D team comprised more than 400
employees, over one-third holding master’s degrees or higher, and held 242 granted patents in the
PRCand43PCTapplicationscoveringautonomousdrivingsystems,drive-by-wireplatforms,cloud
control and dispatch algorithms. Our capabilities have also been recognized internationally,
including ranking first in motion forecasting at the Argoverse 2 Challenge. We follow a full-cycle
R&D framework spanning early-stage research, deployment evaluation, product design and
algorithm development, with core algorithms developed in-house and strategic OEM co-
development of vehicle platforms, supported by enterprise-level IP protection and data security
measures.
MARKETING AND BRANDING
We primarily drive customer acquisition through a direct sales model, building long-term
partnerships with mining companies and contractors. In our early stages, we deployed our own
autonomous fleets to demonstrate safety and accelerate adoption, transitioning over time to
customer-led expansion.
We view brand strength as a key growth driver. Our strategy combines technology
innovations, multi-channel exposure, and strategic communications, including collaboration with
leading universities, participation in industry exhibitions, and engagement with mining and new
energy leaders, to reinforce credibility, trust, and market influence.
OUR CUSTOMERS
We primarily serve mining companies and their contractors, who are the end users of our
autonomous driving solutions. These customers are typically large state-owned or major private
mining firms, with rigorous technical standards and strong commitments to automation and digital
transformation. We focus on customers with high technological acceptance and solid financial
profiles, enabling us to scale pilot deployments into multi-site rollouts. Benchmark deployments at
sites with strong local presence help drive broader adoption. During the Track Record Period, new
customers were primarily acquired through referrals, which accounted for over 91.3% of total
revenue, and we served 13, 24, and 52 customers in 2023, 2024, and 2025, respectively.
In limited cases, mining trucks are purchased by mine owners rather than contractors. This is
because some mine owners operate their mining projects directly, either on their own or through
group companies. For these mine owners, truck ownership forms part of their self-operated
production arrangements. These mine owners are therefore willing to bear the related depreciation
andassetownershipcostsbecausetheyretaincontrolovertheminingassets,scheduleandoperating
process. This customer type has historically represented a relatively small portion of our revenue,
as our principal customers remain contractors.
Mining transport systems require high safety, uptime, and customization, making supplier
switching costly. Our solutions are tightly integrated with vehicle hardware, resulting in high
retention and repeat purchase rates. As of December 31, 2025, nearly all deployments were
multi-phase, with fleet expansion under the same customer.

We believe our relationship with Customer H is mutually beneficial and performance-driven.
As the principal general contractor for multiple large-scale mining sites in Northwest China,
Customer H plays a critical role in the regional deployment of mining autonomous driving
solutions. According to publicly available information, Customer H has become one of the largest
technology-driven mining contractors in the country, especially Northwest China. For us to
participate in major deployments in the region, we consider it commercially and operationally
necessary to engage with Customer H. Likewise, while maintaining strategic partnerships with
several major enterprises that are listed companies for the procurement of mining equipment and
autonomous driving solutions, Customer H has continued to select our solutions due to their
demonstrated reliability, scalability, and cost-effectiveness.
ThesignificantincreaseinrevenuefromCustomerHbetween2023and2024canbeattributed
to several key factors. The engagement evolved from a pilot program to a full-scale deployment.
After initially adopting our solutions on a smaller scale in 2023, Customer H expanded its
partnership in 2024, deploying a significantly larger fleet of autonomous mining trucks across
multiple sites where they acted as a contractor. This growth also reflects Customer H’s recognition
of our technical capabilities and track record, as our solutions have consistently delivered
reliability, scalability, and cost-effectiveness in complex mining environments. Furthermore,
Customer H’s position as the leading contractor for large-scale open-pit mining projects in
Northwest China provided the opportunity to expand our solutions across its mining sites, driving
both deployments and revenues. This revenue increase aligns with our commercialization strategy,
which prioritizes deep technical integration with high-quality customers rather than pursuing
fragmented customer acquisition.
During the Track Record Period, both of our solutions, i.e. (i) Closed-Environment
Autonomous Mining Trucks Products and Solutions (including customer-provided fleet and
Company-provided fleet models) and (ii) Mining Digitalization Solutions, were deployed in
multiple open-pit coal mines where Customer H acted as a contractor. The number of active
autonomous mining trucks at these sites vary, depending on each site’s operational capacity and
deployment phase. Specifically, 143, 347 and 788 active autonomous mining trucks, respectively,
were deployed in these mining sites as of December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025. In addition, the
cumulative annual volume of materials transported at these mining sites was approximately 3.4
million cubic-meters, 81.4 million cubic-meters and 146.1 million cubic-meters for the years ended
December 31, 2023, 2024 and 2025, respectively. These figures appear to indicate that the growth
in transported volumes did not increase in proportion to the growth in the number of active
autonomous trucks. Nonetheless, we believe that this disproportion is primarily attributable to the
varying ramp-up stages, utilization levels and operating conditions across Customer H’s mining
sites during the relevant years, and that Customer H’s adoption of our solutions was generally
commensurate with its growing scale of operation during the same period. The growing safety
requirementsintheminingsectorhavedriventheincreaseddemandforminingautonomousdriving
solutions in 2023. Consistent with industry practice for first-time deployments of mining
autonomous driving solutions, our initial cooperation with Customer H was conducted on a limited
scale to allow for technical validation and operational integration, and as Customer H gained
confidence in the reliability and performance of our solutions, supported by our track record in
early-stage deployments, it progressively expanded the scope and scale of its adoption across
additional mining sites. In addition, the utilization level of the autonomous mining trucks at
Customer H’s mining sites has generally increased during theTrack Record Period and has reached
a level where all such trucks are fully allocated to active production operations.

OUR SUPPLIERS
We collaborate with a broad network of suppliers, providing essential components such as
chassis, mining trucks, maintenance accessories, controllers, batteries, and other critical equipment
required to deliver our solutions. We have built a multi-layer supplier system by working with top
mining equipment manufacturers and specialist parts suppliers, enabling us to deliver stable and
reliable solutions to our customers.
The following sets forth salient terms of standard agreements with our suppliers:
 Product and Service Specification. The contracts set forth specific name, model, price,
quantity and other detailed characteristics of the products ordered, as well as the price
and scope of manufacturing, equipment and other ancillary services provided.
 Payment. Our payment terms generally include an initial prepayment following contract
effectiveness, with the remaining balance payable after delivery and acceptance in
accordance with the agreed timeline.

 Delivery and Acceptance. Suppliers are required to deliver the products which are
completed with manufacturing, equipment or other services, and we are required to

 Warranty. Suppliers are generally responsible for providing free repair services during
the warranty period, as well as ongoing technical support and consultation, in
accordance with the terms agreed in the contract. Major suppliers typically offer
warranties based on a defined warranty schedule, while original equipment
manufacturers provide component-level warranties subject to time-based, generally up
to mileage-based limits, generally up to 200,000 miles, and other major suppliers
generally offer warranties for around 36 months.
 Quality Control. Suppliers shall ensure that the products provided are new and comply

standards, at the supplier’s expense.

Supply Chain and Inventory Management
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we did not experience

restrictions.Tomitigateriskandenhanceflexibility,weactivelymanagesupplierconcentrationand

ENVIRONMENTAL, SOCIAL, AND GOVERNANCE
ESG Governance Framework
We fully recognize the critical role of environmental and social responsibility in shaping
business success.To drive ESG execution, we established a dedicated ESGTask Force, coordinated
by the Internal Control Department and involving cross-functional teams.
Post-IPO, we plan to form an ESG Committee, reporting to the Board of Directors. This
committee will oversee the effective implementation of ESG policies, track ESG performance
metrics, refine strategic direction as needed, and ensure ESG disclosures align with applicable laws
and regulations.
Board Diversity
Our Board of Directors consists of nine members, structured to balance deep expertise with
diverse perspectives for effective governance. Looking ahead, we aim to further enhance diversity
and inclusion to strengthen corporate governance and long-term sustainability. Our board of
directors comprises members with diverse backgrounds in terms of age, gender, education, and
professional experience. Collectively, they bring expertise across key areas such as investment,
technology and corporate management, and have accumulated extensive industry experience.
Product Responsibility & Customer Value
Asapioneerinautonomousmining,weprioritizecustomervaluecreation,drivingoperational
transformation through intelligent automation.
 Enhanced Safety: Harsh mining environments present unpredictable terrain and
operational hazards. By deeply integrating autonomous driving with smart safety
systems, we eliminate human risk factors. We have achieved a six-year zero-casualty
safety record, according to Frost & Sullivan, which validates our commitment to “safety
through autonomy”.
 Greater Efficiency: Our 24/7 unmanned operations integrate smart dispatch algorithms
for dynamic route optimization, reducing transport distances versus manual driving.
Each autonomous truck operates up to 110% of human-driven efficiency, and excels in
adverse weather conditions, including rain, fog, snow, and dust storms, ensuring
continuousandefficientoperations.Bydeployingminingautonomousdrivingsolutions,
we reduce labor costs by approximately 80% in 2024, as compared to non-autonomous
mining operations, significantly improving overall mining productivity.
 Green Transition: Our new-energy propulsion systems, paired with AI- driven route
optimization and intelligent energy management, enable sustainable mining transport.
For example, our extended-range EL100 autonomous mining truck delivers a 25-30%
– 166 –

=== PAGE 176 ===
BUSINESS
improvement in fuel efficiency compared to traditional diesel models, and our
battery-electric models further saves energy costs by over 60% relative to our own
extended-range autonomous mining trucks.
 Sustainable Workforce Transformation: Mining sites are often in remote regions,
requiring continuous operations. Labor shortages remain a persistent issue, exacerbated
by an aging workforce. Through automation, we systematically address labor
constraints, reducing onsite driver demand while transitioning personnel to higher-value
roles such as remote dispatch operations and equipment maintenance.
Climate Action Strategies
Governance & Oversight
We integrate green development into corporate strategy and operations, driving cross-
departmental emissions reduction initiatives across HR, Engineering, and R&D. We will further
refine climate governance, defining Board and executive oversight roles in environmental risk
management.
Risk & Opportunity
Analysis Climate risks — both physical and transitional — directly impact our operational
footprint and influence infrastructure resilience and financial planning. As global decarbonization
accelerates, we must expand R&D investments in low-carbon technologies and upgrade assets to
mitigate transition risks.
Metrics & Targets
Amid growing global focus on climate change and the energy transition, we are advancing
energy-efficient technologies and accelerating the development of new-energy autonomous driving
solutions. These efforts are aligned with China’s “30-60” carbon reduction goals and contribute
meaningfully to industry-wide decarbonization and emissions reduction.

operating fleet, accelerating the shift toward clean-energy haulage solutions. Second, we target a
30% reduction in greenhouse gas (GHG) emission intensity by 2030, using 2024 as our baseline
year. These targets reflect our commitment to aligning business growth with environmental
responsibility and supporting the broader low-carbon transition of the mining industry.
We have set long-term carbon reduction goals centered on lowering energy consumption and
emission intensity across our operations. A key element of this plan is the large-scale adoption of
new-energy mining trucks and the establishment of measurable emission reduction milestones for

We have adopted a wide range of ESG policies covering environmental compliance, resource
efficiency, clean transportation, and waste management:
– Resource efficiency: We refurbish and reuse faulty autonomous vehicle components,
operate a centralized warehouse to better allocate materials, and make use of reusable

– Cleantransportationandairquality:WearerollingoutEVchargingstationsinparking

systems to prevent leakage and residual pollution. We also mitigate dust and exhaust
emissions by installing suppression systems, sprinkling water in work zones, and
enforcing strict controls on vehicle exhaust.

Talent Development & Training
We are committed to building a robust talent development system, offering competitive
compensation and benefits while establishing a postdoctoral research program to cultivate
high-level industry expertise. Our clear career progression framework ensures employees have
well-defined growth opportunities, and we conduct company-wide satisfaction surveys to
proactively address employee concerns. We also prioritize physical and mental well-being,
organizing regular sports activities and providing housing subsidies, medical check-ups, and
holiday support packages.
Occupational Health and Safety
Mining transportation has always been a high-risk area for accidents. We have implemented
a comprehensive safety accountability system built around risk tiering and clearly defined
responsibilities. Our safety framework covers risk identification across four operational scenarios,
including mixed traffic involving manned and unmanned vehicles, electric truck operations, and
autonomous haulage. Our self-developed autonomous driving system is designed to completely
remove the need for drivers in high-risk areas like deep pits and slopes, ensuring the safety of
personnel from the start. By using an intelligent system that connects the vehicle, energy, road, and
cloud, we eliminate traditional safety risks faced by drivers and significantly reduce accident rates.
In April 2025, we obtained ISO 45001 Occupational Health and Safety Management System
certification. In addition, to ensure the well-being of our employees, we offer competitive and
steadily increasing salaries, along with various benefits such as five social insurances, one housing
fund, commercial insurance, holiday benefits, and project subsidies. We strive to create a simple,
focused, and dynamic working environment. To support both the company’s and employees’
growth, and to help employees adapt their knowledge and skills to changing technologies and the
external environment, we provide on-the-job training, college courses, industry visits, and free
further education and exams as part of our training and education benefits.
Responsible Supply Chain Management
Oursuppliermanagementprogramcoverstheentirelifecycle,fromsourcingandqualification
to performance review and offboarding, governed by detailed internal policies and standard
operating procedures. ESG considerations are integrated into our procurement process, with
particular focus on product quality, energy efficiency, ethical labor practices, and anti-corruption.
New suppliers are screened for compliance with standards such as CCC, RoHS, ISO certifications,
and are required to provide declarations on human rights and business ethics.
Anti-Corruption and Ethics
Wehaveestablishedarobustcomplianceinfrastructurewithclearanti-briberyandanti-money
laundering policies. Key controls include segregation of duties, regular risk assessments, and audit
mechanisms across procurement and sales workflows.
All employees are required to sign ethics pledges, and we mandate anti-corruption clauses in
contracts with business partners. Regular compliance training and testing are conducted across the
organization, and periodic anti-bribery audits are performed, with findings publicly reported within
the company.
We also maintain a robust compliance framework designed to prevent bribery, fraud, and
money laundering. This framework includes ourAnti-Bribery andAnti-Fraud Management System
andAnti-Money Laundering Management System.We provide multiple reporting channels, such as
email, letters, our corporate website, and our official WeChat account, to enable employees and
business partners to report potential misconduct. Reports are investigated by a dedicated internal
team, which has authority to take appropriate action.

QUALITY CONTROL
Weregardproductandsolutionqualityasacorecompetitiveadvantageandhaveimplemented
a comprehensive quality management system spanning R&D, system integration, delivery, and
after-salesservice.Standardizedprocessesandcontinuousimprovement,reinforcedbymanagement
reviews, ensure alignment with evolving business and technology needs.
We maintain rigorous quality controls at critical stages, including vehicle assembly, site
deployment, and operational safety assessments. All systems undergo multi-layered testing
covering functional performance, system stability, module interoperability, and emergency fallback
mechanisms, simulating harsh mining conditions such as dust, steep gradients, and mixed traffic.
Our practices enable consistent, reliable solutions that meet stringent safety standards.We are
among the first in China’s mining autonomous driving sector certified under ISO 26262 ASIL D,
integrating over 4,000 intelligent diagnostic checks and providing five-fold safety redundancy to
ensure stable performance in high-risk environments.
Product Return and Warranty Policies
For our mining autonomous driving solutions deployed on the trucks possessed by our
customers, we provide routine maintenance and inspection services to support the continued
performance of our mining autonomous driving solutions in accordance with the scope and the
conditions set forth in the contract.
If the customers purchase the autonomous mining trucks from us, we provide solid after-sales
services based on the warranty clauses set forth in our sales contracts. Upon notice from our
customers, we confirm relevant information with them and arrange inspection, repair or
replacement accordingly. If our autonomous mining trucks or related hardware is confirmed to be
non-conforming for quality issues, we provide maintenance, repair or replacement services free of
charge. Our agreements with OEMs generally include warranty provisions that require the OEMs
to provide maintenance and repair services to our customers under terms comparable to what we
offer to our customers. During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we
did not experience any material product returns or warranty issues due to the quality of our
offerings. During theTrack Record Period and up to the Last Practicable Date, there were no safety
incidents, complaints lodged formally with us or authorities, product recalls, or reports of injury or
fatality associated with our solutions or autonomous mining trucks.
INFORMATION SECURITY AND DATA MANAGEMENT
As we serve large mining enterprises rather than individual consumers, we do not collect
personal information from third parties except for necessary contact details. Any data processed
during R&D, particularly for autonomous driving and system optimization, is handled in
compliance with applicable laws. We collaborate with qualified partners to anonymize datasets,
ensuring all data is secured and privacy-compliant.
We maintain a comprehensive information security framework covering policy development,
access controls, technical safeguards, and risk assessments to protect the confidentiality, integrity,
and availability of operational data. Employees are bound by confidentiality obligations, and
sensitive roles require non-compete agreements.We also prohibit the use of unauthorized software.
Based on consultation with the CCRC and advice from our PRC Legal Advisor, we have not
been classified as a CIIO, are not required to file a cybersecurity review, and have not received any
notices, investigations, or sanctions from PRC authorities. We consider the likelihood of a
cybersecurity review in connection with our Hong Kong listing to be low, and our practices are
consistent with the Cybersecurity Review Measures.
AsconfirmedbyourDirectors,ourdataisstoredonserverslocatedwithinChinesemainland,
with relevant systems operating under strict access controls.As of the Latest Practicable Date, we
are not aware of any outbound transfer of data collected or generated through operations within the
PRC that would trigger the application of the Measures on Security Assessment of Outbound Data
Transfer. Based on the foregoing, our PRC Legal Advisor is of the view that, as of the Latest
Practicable Date, we were not required to undergo a security assessment for outbound data transfer.

encryption system that automatically encrypts all files generated on our terminals, including source
code and technical documents. These encrypted files cannot be externally transferred without
authorization and are protected by role-based access controls and centralized key management.The
DLPsystem also enables centralized oversight of software usage and file access, further enhancing
system-level data protection.
We maintain full control over core system development and operation, ensuring long-term
security and stability. To enhance cybersecurity, we regularly engage third-party security firms for
penetration tests, audits, and red-teaming exercises, using findings to drive targeted system
upgrades.These measures strengthen ITadaptability and resilience, supporting business expansion,
operational efficiency, and our digital transformation strategy.
Our PRC Legal Advisor is of the view that, during the Track Record Period and up to the
Latest Practicable Date, all of our personal and operational data collection and processes involved
in our business operations comply in material respects with the requirements of the applicable PRC
laws and regulations relating to data privacy, cybersecurity and personal data protection.
BUSINESS SUSTAINABILITY AND PATH TO PROFITABILITY
We have recorded net loss during theTrack Record Period and expect to continue to incur net
losses in the near term. We first deployed our solutions to our customers in mining sites in July
2020, starting from capital-intensive mining transportation operations. We had accumulated loss as
of January 1, 2022, primarily because the heavy upfront investment associated with the
Company-provided fleet model at the early stages, our sustained research and development efforts
to establish the technological foundation of our mining autonomous driving solutions, and the
relatively high customer acquisition costs associated with entering a nascent industry. Our projects
are primarily located in sparsely populated mining areas and are operated through centralized
remote management, which significantly reduced exposure to pandemic-related disruptions such as
travelrestrictions,quarantinerequirements,andlaborshortages.Inaddition,weadoptedaproactive
market expansion strategy during the early phase of commercialization, prioritizing rapid
deployment and broad coverage to secure high-quality customers, which further increased our
initial cost of revenue. The trend continued to the beginning of the Track Record Period and led to
our gross loss margin incurred in 2023. In 2023, 2024 and 2025, we incurred losses of RMB333.7
million, RMB390.1 million, and RMB515.6 million respectively. Our adjusted net loss (non-
HKFRS measure) for these years was RMB283.9 million, RMB303.3 million, and RMB484.5
million, respectively. These losses reflect deliberate and strategic investments we made to lay the
technological and commercial foundation for long-term development in the mining autonomous
driving solution sector. Specifically, our gross losses in 2023 primarily reflected a combination of
relatively low service fee rates during the early stage of commercialization, high depreciation
expenses associated with our autonomous mining trucks, and the timing mismatch between the
recognition of costs and revenues, as certain upfront costs were incurred early in the project cycle,
whereas the revenue generated from services fees was recognized over time as our services were
delivered. These factors also collectively contributed to our relatively thin gross margin for 2024
and 2025. Despite of that, the increase in net loss from 2024 to 2025 was also affected by an
impairmentlossrecognizedonassetsclassifiedasheldforsaleofRMB118.4million,insteadofany
fundamental weakening of our underlying business performance. We expect to break even in terms
of both net profit and operating cash inflow over the next three to five years.

Asacompanyattheintersectionofautonomousdriving,AI,andheavyindustriallogistics,we

We believe our historical loss-making position is attributable to a combination of the
following factors:
 Significant upfront investments to develop full-stack autonomous mining capabilities.
Autonomous mining is not a simple feature upgrade; it requires a ground-up
transformation of how mining sites operate. Our solutions must function in highly
variable,unstructured,andharshenvironments,suchashigh-altitudeopen-pitmines.To
deliver commercial vehicle intelligent driving performance under these conditions, we
made significant upfront investments to build an integrated technology stack, including
our Yushi, our proprietary drive-by-wire electronic controlling platform designed
specifically for mining applications; a modular Intelligent Driving OS; redundant
vehicle control systems; and a universal safety framework. These capabilities could not
be sourced through commercially available solutions and required years of in-house
development and iterative refinement. As of December 31, 2025, our R&D team
included more than 400 employees, with over one third holding master’s degrees or
higher. As of the same date, we had 242 granted patents in the PRC as well as 43 PCT
applications, and completed more than 100 software releases across major architectural
generations.
 Early commercialization through capital-intensive Company-provided fleet model. To
accelerate early adoption and reduce customer concerns around unmanned operations,
we initially adopted a Company-provided fleet model under which we supplied and
operatedourownautonomoustruckfleets.Thisallowedcustomerstoadoptoursolution
with minimal upfront commitment, while enabling us to validate performance under
real-world conditions. However, the Company-provided fleet model is capital- and
labor-intensive, requiring significant upfront investment in vehicle procurement, as well
as ongoing costs related to fuel consumption, vehicle depreciation, on-site engineering
teams, and technical support.As a result, margins under this model were relatively low.
In 2024, revenue under the Company-provided fleet model accounted for 52.7% of our
total revenue.
Looking forward, we expect to achieve sustainable profitability through a combination of
business model transformation, revenue scale, and cost optimization:
 Expanding our customer base through benchmark deployments and strategic
partnerships. Our core business strategy focuses on securing high-visibility benchmark
deployments that demonstrate the technical viability of our solutions and serve as proof
points to drive broader customer adoption. For example, our successful deployment at
one of China’s largest coal mines has led to expansion across within the mining site
portfolio of its end customer group, while Zijin Mining began scaling our solution from
the Zijinshan site to the high-altitude Julong copper mine. These benchmark cases
illustrate our ability to deliver results under varied and demanding conditions. See “—
Case Studies”.

SEASONALITY
Our business is subject to seasonal patterns due to the nature of mining operations in the
regions where our solutions are deployed. Many of the mining sites where our solutions are
deployed are located in remote regions, often at high latitudes, where harsh winter conditions can
limit site access and slow mining activities. As a result, we typically see a slowdown in solution
deploymentandrevenuerecognitionduringthefirstquarter.Thisseasonalityreflectson-the-ground
operating constraints rather than weakened demand and is consistent with industry dynamics in the
mining sector.

Housing provident fund contributions
In accordance with the Regulations on the Administration of Housing Provident Fund (《住
房公積金管理條例》) and other relevant PRC laws and regulations, employers in China are
required to make housing provident fund contributions for their employees. During the Track
Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not made housing provident fund
contributions for certain employees within their probationary periods as required under applicable
PRC laws and regulations. During theTrack Record Period, the aggregate shortfall of such housing
provident fund contributions amounted to approximately RMB0.7 million. If instructed by the
relevant housing provident fund management center to make full contributions, the maximum
amount we would be required to pay is approximately RMB0.7 million.
AsadvisedbyourPRCLegalAdvisor,whereanemployerisoverdueinmaking,orunderpays,
housing provident fund contributions, the relevant housing provident fund management center may
order the employer to make the outstanding contributions within a prescribed period. If the
employerfailstodosowithintheprescribedperiod,thehousingprovidentfundmanagementcenter
may apply to a PRC court for compulsory enforcement.
During the Track Record Period and up to the Latest Practicable Date, we had not received
any notice from local authorities, nor any claims or requests from affected employees, requiring
rectification, imposing administrative penalties or demanding payment in respect of such historical
under-contributions to housing provident funds. However, we cannot assure you that the relevant
authorities will not subsequently require us to make retroactive payments or impose late payment
charges or administrative fines. If we are required to make additional payments or are subject to
penalties, our business, financial condition and results of operations may be adversely affected.
We have taken, and will continue to take, internal control measures to improve our housing
provident fund contribution practices and minimize the recurrence of similar non-compliance. In
particular, we are strengthening the coordination between our human resources and finance
departments to identify employees who are required to participate in the housing provident fund
scheme upon commencement of employment, including employees within their probationary
periods. We have also enhanced our onboarding procedures by providing employees with
explanationsoftheapplicablehousingprovidentfundrequirementsandthecontributionprocess.In
addition, we have established internal review procedures to monitor the status of housing provident

U.S. OUTBOUND INVESTMENT PROGRAM
The U.S. government has established a China-focused outbound investment regulatory
framework that imposes prohibitions and notification requirements on certain transactions by U.S.
persons involving entities associated with countries of concern, including China, Hong Kong and
Macau, in specified technology sectors. OnAugust 9, 2023, the U.S. government issued Executive
Order 14105, titled “Addressing United States Investments in Certain National Security
TechnologiesandProductsinCountriesofConcern”(“E.O.14105”).OnOctober28,2024,theU.S.
Department of the Treasury (“Treasury”) issued a final rule implementing E.O. 14105 (the “Final
Rule”; and such program as in effect on the date hereof pursuant to the Final Rule, the “OISP”),
whichtookeffectonJanuary2,2025.TheOISPappliestocertaintransactionsbyU.S.persons,and
certain transactions involving their non-U.S. subsidiaries, in three technology sectors:
semiconductors and microelectronics, quantum information technologies and artificial intelligence
systems.
The OISP applies to certain U.S. person transactions involving “Covered Foreign Persons,”
which generally include companies that are engaged in specified activities in the relevant
technology sectors and have certain jurisdictional or ownership connections with a country of
concern, as well as companies with significant financial ties to such companies. Depending on the
relevant technology, activity and transaction structure, a transaction may be prohibited or subject
to a notification requirement. U.S. persons’ purchases of certain publicly traded securities are
generally neither prohibited nor subject to notification under the Final Rule, provided that the
relevant conditions under the publicly traded securities exception are satisfied. On December 23,
2025,TreasurypublishedadditionalFAQsregardingthescopeofthisexception,includingguidance
that may be relevant to IPO offerings.
The OISP imposes investment (1) prohibitions and (2) notification requirements on certain
actions by U.S. persons, including the extent to which such U.S. persons (including, among others,
U.S.-incorporated entities, U.S. citizens and permanent residents wherever located, branches of
U.S.entitiesoutsidetheUnitedStates,andanypersonintheUnitedStates)ortheirnon-U.S.person
subsidiaries participate in, or seek to participate in, a range of transactions relating to three
technology sectors: (i) semiconductors and microelectronics, (ii) quantum information
technologies, and (iii) artificial intelligence systems. As advised by our legal advisor as to U.S.
outbound investment laws, our Directors are of the view that: (i) we are a Covered Foreign Person
since we are organized under the laws of the PRC and, based on our current business operations,
we are engaged in the development of AI-enabled autonomous driving systems for mining
applications, which may constitute “covered activities” under the AI systems category under the
OIP; (ii) we are not engaged in activities described in the definition of “Prohibited Transaction”
under the OIP, because we do not design, develop, or produceAI systems intended exclusively for
military,intelligence,orotherendusesexpresslycontemplatedasprohibitedundertheOIP,andwe
are not engaged in covered semiconductor or quantum computing activities that would fall within
the prohibited categories; and (iii) nevertheless, our business activities are likely to fall within the
definition of a “Notifiable Transaction” because our solutions comprise perception and decision-
making modules that fuse real-time sensor inputs and generate executable commands that
physically control mining trucks’ operation (e.g., overtaking, and logistics optimization) within
miningenvironments.AsadvisedbyourlegaladvisorastoU.S.outboundinvestmentlaws,because
the OIP includes AI systems intended for the “control of robotic systems,” and “robotic systems”
is not further defined in the regulation, it cannot be excluded that the Treasury could interpret
unmanned mining trucks as falling within that notifiable end-use category, depending on the facts
and any future guidance. Based on the due diligence work conducted by the Sole Sponsor, the Sole
Sponsor concurs with the aforementioned views of the Directors. Accordingly, if no exception is
available, U.S. persons that purchase our Shares in the Global Offering, or U.S. persons that are the
parent of a non-U.S. person that purchases our Shares in the Global Offering who bear the
responsibility to report a Notifiable Transaction under the Final Rule, rather than us, may be
required to submit a notification to Treasury no later than 30 days after the relevant purchase.
As advised by our legal advisor as to U.S. outbound investment laws, our Directors are of the
view that upon the completion of the Global Offering, U.S. persons are allowed to purchase our
publiclytradedsharesregardlessofthefactthatwewillbeconsideredasaCoveredForeignPerson,
given that U.S. persons’ purchases of certain publicly traded securities are neither prohibited nor
require notification to Treasury under an exception in the Final Rule that applies to U.S. persons’
purchase of “any publicly traded security, with ‘security’ as defined in the U.S. Exchange Act,
denominatedinanycurrency,andthattradesonasecuritiesexchangeinanyjurisdiction”,provided
such U.S. persons or their non-U.S. person subsidiaries are not afforded rights beyond standard
minorityshareholderprotectionswithrespecttotherelevantCoveredForeignPerson(the“Publicly
TradedSecuritiesException”).BasedontheduediligenceworkconductedbytheSoleSponsor,the
Sole Sponsor concurs with the aforementioned views of the Directors.

The outbound investment framework may continue to evolve. For example, President Trump

ortheCOINSAct,thatcodifiesandexpandstheoutboundinvestmentframework.Ifsimilarormore

results of operations and prospects, may be adversely affected.

INDEPENDENCE FROM OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
Having considered the following factors, our Directors are satisfied that we are capable of
carrying on our business independently of our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates
after Listing.
Management Independence
We are able to carry on our business independently from the Controlling Shareholders from
a management perspective. Our Board will consist of nine Directors, including five executive
Directors, one non-executive Director and three independent non-executive Directors upon Listing.
Our executive Directors and senior management team are responsible for the day-to-day
management of our operations. Notwithstanding the roles of Mr. Lan and Mr. Zhang in our Board
andourseniormanagementteam,ourDirectorsareoftheviewthatourCompanyisabletofunction
independently from the Controlling Shareholders for the following reasons:
(a) all of the independent non-executive Directors are independent of the Controlling
Shareholders. Our independent non-executive Directors have extensive experience in
different areas.We believe that they will be able to exercise their independent judgment
and will be able to provide impartial opinions in the decision-making process of our
Board to protect the interests of our Shareholders;
(b) each Director is aware of his/her fiduciary duties as a director which require, among
other things, that he/she acts for the benefit and in the interest of our Company and does
notallowanyconflictbetweenhis/herdutiesasaDirectorandhis/herpersonalinterests;
(c) our daily management and operations are carried out by our senior management team,
all of whom have substantial experience in the industry in which our Company is
engaged, and will therefore be able to make business decisions that are in the best
interests of our Group;
(d) where a Board meeting or Shareholders’ meeting is held to consider a proposed
transactioninwhichourDirectorsorControllingShareholdersoranyoftheirrespective
close associates have a material interest, the relevant Directors or our Controlling
Shareholders and their respective close associates shall abstain from voting on the
relevant resolutions and shall not be counted towards the quorum for the voting; and
– 193 –

=== PAGE 203 ===
RELATIONSHIP WITH OUR CONTROLLING SHAREHOLDERS
(e) we have adopted a series of corporate governance measures to manage conflicts of
interest, if any, between our Group and the Controlling Shareholders which would
support our independent management, in accordance with our Articles, relevant
corporate governance policies and the Listing Rules as well as other applicable rules,
laws and regulations.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that our Board as a whole and together with our
senior management are able to perform the managerial role in our Group independently from the
Controlling Shareholders and their close associates after the Listing.
Operational Independence
Our Company has full rights to make all decisions on and to carry out for our own business
development, staffing, logistics, administration, finance, internal audit, information technology,
salesandmarketing,orcompanysecretarialfunctions.Wehaveindependentaccesstosuppliersand
customers and an independent management team to handle our day-to-day operations. We are also
inpossessionofallrelevantlicensesnecessarytocarryonandoperateourprincipalbusinesses,and
we have sufficient operational capacity in terms of capital and employees to operate independently.
We have our own departments specializing in these respective areas which have been in operation
and are expected to continue to operate separately and independently from the Controlling
Shareholders and their close associates. In addition, we have our own headcount of employees for
our operations and management for human resources.
Based on the above, our Directors believe that we are able to operate independently from the
Controlling Shareholders and their close associates.
Financial Independence
Our Group has a finance department independent from our Controlling Shareholders and their
respective close associates. We have also established an independent financial system to make the
decisionsbasedonourownbusinessneeds.Moreover,ourGroupopensandmanagesbankaccounts
independently, and has never shared any bank account with Controlling Shareholders. Our Group
has independent taxation registration according to the relevant laws, and makes tax payments
independently according to the applicable PRC taxation laws and regulations.
As of the Latest Practicable Date, there is no outstanding loan extended by our Controlling
Shareholders and/or their close associates to us. Any guarantee previously provided by the
Controlling Shareholders and/or their close associate(s) for our benefit has been released.
In view of our internal resources, our undrawn banking facilities, our net cash generated from
operating activities and the estimated net proceeds from the Global Offering, our Directors confirm
that we will not rely on our Controlling Shareholders for financing support after the Global
Offering. Our Directors also believe that, upon Listing, the sustainability of our business — as
demonstrated by our results of operations and financial position during the Track Record Period —
will enhance our ability to obtain or renew loans and borrowings from banks on an independent
basis without the support of the Controlling Shareholders.
Based on the above, our Directors are of the view that we are able to maintain financial
independence from our Controlling Shareholders and their close associates.

OurCompanywillcomplywiththeprovisionsoftheCorporateGovernanceCodeinAppendix
C1 to the Listing Rules, which sets out principles of good corporate governance.
Our Directors recognize the importance of good corporate governance in protection of our
Shareholders’ interests. We would adopt the following measures to safeguard good corporate
governance standards and to avoid potential conflict of interests between our Group and the
Controlling Shareholders:
(a) where a Shareholders’ meeting is to be held for considering proposed transactions in
which the Controlling Shareholders or any of their respective associates has a material
interest, the Controlling Shareholders will not vote on the resolutions and shall not be
counted in the quorum in the voting;

(b) our Company has established internal control mechanisms to identify connected
transactions. Upon the Listing, if our Company enters into connected transactions with
aControllingShareholderoranyofhis/itsassociates,ourCompanywillcomplywiththe

approval;
(c) our Board consists of a balanced composition of executive, non-executive and

various requirements relating to corporate governance.

Shareholders, and to protect minority Shareholders’ interests after the Listing.

products and services, and changes in the number or models of autonomous mining
trucks deployed by us.
Overall, the annual cap for transactions contemplated under the Lanbang Products and
Services Sales FrameworkAgreement is expected to decline from 2026 to 2028.The annual cap for
2027 and 2028 are expected to remain broadly consistent. This stability reflects the shift in focus
toward providing related products and services to support the operation of autonomous mining
trucks, rather than generating revenue from the sale of autonomous mining trucks. The decrease in
annual cap is more pronounced from 2026 to 2027, and across the 2026–2028 period overall,
primarily reflecting the expected decrease of one-off sales of autonomous mining truck in 2027 in
light of uncertainty for the pipeline of mining projects acquired and operated by relevant parties in
a relatively longer period. However, the Group will continue to provide related products and
services for operation of autonomous mining trucks in 2026, 2027 and 2028 at a stable level, which
is not expected to experience material fluctuations compared to the one-off sales of autonomous
mining trucks.

INTERNAL CONTROL PROCEDURES ADOPTED BY THE COMPANY IN RESPECT OF
THE CONTINUING CONNECTED TRANSACTION AGREEMENTS
In order to further safeguard the interests of the Shareholders as a whole (including the
minority Shareholders), our Group has implemented the following internal control measures in
relation to the continuing connected transactions:
 Our Group has approved internal guidelines which provide that if the value of any
proposed connected transaction is expected to exceed certain thresholds, the relevant
staffmustreporttheproposedtransactionstotherelevantresponsiblepersonnelinorder
for our Company to commence the necessary additional assessment and approval
procedures and ensure that we will comply with the applicable requirements under
Chapter 14A of the Listing Rules.
 Our Company will provide information and supporting documents to the independent
non-executive Directors and the auditors in order for them to conduct an annual review
of the continuing connected transactions entered into by our Company. In accordance
with the requirements under the Listing Rules, the independent non-executive Directors
willprovideanannualconfirmationtotheBoardastowhetherthecontinuingconnected
transactions have been entered into in the ordinary and usual course of business of our
Group, are on normal commercial terms and are in accordance with the agreement
governing them on terms that are fair and reasonable and in the interests of the
Shareholders as a whole, and the auditors will provide an annual confirmation to the
Boardastowhetheranythinghascometotheirattentionthatcausesthemtobelievethat
the continuing connected transactions have not been approved by the Board, are not in
accordancewiththepricingpoliciesofourGroupinallmaterialrespects,arenotentered
into in accordance with the relevant agreements governing the transactions in all
material respects or have exceeded the cap as stated above.
 When considering any renewal or revisions to the agreements after Listing, the
interested Directors and Shareholders shall abstain from voting on the resolutions to
approve such transactions at board meetings or shareholders’ general meetings (as the

cannot be obtained, we will not continue the transactions under the framework
agreement(s) to the extent that they constitute non-exempt continuing connected
transactions under Rule 14A.35 of the Listing Rules.

KEY FACTORS AFFECTING OUR RESULTS OF OPERATIONS
Our business, financial condition and results of operations are subject to a variety of factors,
many of which are beyond our control. These factors have had, and are expected to continue to
have, a meaningful impact on our performance.
General Factors
Our performance depends in part on the overall development of the mining and mining
autonomous driving sectors, including: (i) macroeconomic conditions in China and globally, and
overall investment and production trends in the mining sector; (ii) government policies, industry
initiatives and incentives that encourage autonomous driving and automated transformation of
mining operations; (iii) the market acceptance and adoption of mining autonomous driving and
technologies;(iv)advancesinautonomousdrivingtechnologies,miningautomationandnewenergy
transportation systems; and (v) the competitive landscape and market dynamics within the
commercial vehicle intelligent driving industry.
Company-specific Factors
Our Ability to Grow Our Customer Base and Deepen Existing Relationships
Our growth depends on our ability to expand our customer base and strengthen our
relationships with major mining companies and contractors.
We serve the largest and most prominent and forward-thinking mining corporations in China,
includingCHNEnergy,SPIC,TBEA,ZijinMining,ShougangGroup,GuanghuiEnergy,andBaowu
Group. As of December 31, 2025, we had 13 end customer groups across 30 mining sites. The
number of our end customer groups grew from five as of December 31, 2023 to ten as of December
31, 2024, with strong customer stickiness reflected in the 100% retention rate for all of our end
customer groups for three consecutive years from 2023 to 2025. In addition, as of December 31,
2025, the fleet deployed at a single mining site where our solutions are in operation has grown to
over 500 autonomous mining trucks, representing the largest autonomous mining truck fleet
deployed at a single mine globally. This expansion reflects our customers’ continued confidence in
our solutions and their ongoing expansion of deployments with us as their operations scale.

Our Ability to Innovate and Upgrade Our Technologies and Solutions
Technology innovation and continuous solution enhancement are central to our business,
expandingourmarketshare,anddrivinglong-termprofitability.Ourabilitytoconsistentlyinnovate
and upgrade directly impacts our financial performance in several ways:
 Strengthening solution competitiveness and supporting revenue growth: Superior
technologyallowsustodeliverhigher-performancesolutionsthatmeettherequirements
of large and complex mining deployments.This strengthens our competitive positioning
with leading mining customers and drives revenue growth.
 Enhancing customer loyalty and repeat purchases: By improving operational
performance,reducingsystemdowntime,andenhancingsafetyoutcomes,westrengthen
customer satisfaction, leading to higher renewal rates and deeper customer penetration.
 Reducing technology displacement and competitive risks: Sustained innovation extends
the lifecycle of our technology platforms, reinforces customer reliance on our solutions,
and strengthens barriers to entry against existing and emerging competitors.
 Expanding addressable markets through broader application scenarios: Ongoing
technological advancement enables us to extend our solutions to more complex mining
environments, such as high-altitude, extreme weather, and rugged terrain sites,
unlocking additional customer demand and expanding our total addressable market.
 Improving delivery efficiency and profitability: Increased standardization,
modularization, and system stability reduce the need for customization, shorten
deployment cycles, and enhance operational efficiency, thereby improving deployment-
level margins and overall operating leverage.
In 2023, 2024 and 2025, our research and development expenses were RMB177.3 million,
RMB208.4 million, and RMB270.5 million, respectively, representing 65.4%, 21.1% and 18.8%
respectively,ofourtotalrevenueforthesameperiods.Havingcompletedfoundationaldevelopment
across our core autonomous driving capabilities, we are currently focused on modular
productization, reusing validated components across different sites, and developing new revenue-
generating features based on customer needs. While we continue to invest in areas such as AI
algorithms research and applications, intelligent production management, and hardware
development, we expect our research and development expenses as a percentage of total revenue to
decline over time in the long term as our deployments scale and customization requirements
decrease. See also “Business — Business Sustainability and Path to Profitability”. As the mining
industry’s transition toward intelligent operations accelerates, our ability to drive algorithm
advancements, enhance system stability, and launch next-generation software-hardware platforms
will be critical to strengthening our competitive position, deepening customer engagement,
supporting revenue growth, and sustaining profitability over the long term.
Our Ability to Manage Hardware Production and Supply Chain Costs
Hardware systems, including autonomous mining trucks, drive-by-wire electronic controlling
chassis platforms, core sensor modules, and autonomous driving domain controllers, are integral to
our solutions. Hardware performance, reliability, and cost efficiency directly affect our ability to
deliver deployments on time, maintain operational stability, and protect margins. We maintain
